title: The formation law is not fixed: no order, rate, unit, or where/when records form

members.title: The formation law is not fixed: one rule, many laws
members.plain: The axiom says a site's odds depend on its neighbours. But neighbours form at different times, so which ones count as already there depends on the order sites form, whether neighbours form together, and how unrecorded sites are treated. Each choice gives a different law from the same rule, and the all-at-once (static) law is none of them once a loop exists. The axioms do not pick the order.

members.title: No rule for where, when and how fast records form
members.plain: The axioms say records form, not at which site, at what rate, or in what numbers. Written as a mathematical birth process, the allowed rules form a whole family (six free rates for a cube-symmetric one), and nothing picks one. What a sealed box freezes into, and whether that is one state or exponentially many, is decided by the rule you supply, not by the axioms.

members.title: The rule does not fix one law: no formation order, rate or unit
members.plain: The axioms say how likely each possibility is at a site once its neighbours are known. They do not say in what order sites get their records. The order matters: different orders give provably different overall laws, and the equilibrium law is none of them. Because the rule looks the same in every direction, no single fixed order can be chosen either. Something must say how records form: a rate, a unit, or a causal order.

attack.plain: The axioms say what a record contains when it forms but not the order sites form in, and different orders give different overall laws, so no single law follows. The gap is exactly one clause; its cheapest form is that the next site is chosen blind to the record state, which has no free numbers and gives one law on all of Z^3, but it is adopted, not derived. A bulk test shows three equally covariant clauses give different local statistics and the blind one never orders, so the choice cannot be waved away.
attack.best_route: Adopt the state-blind single-site clause (independent exchangeable priorities, a reading of AX:40-41 and AX:57); Lemma B shows it is the only projective hazard f(k), k<=5; cost: no ordered phase and no gated frozen box.
attack.test: Monte Carlo on 3D tori (L up to 16) validated against exact plaquette values and the static threshold 3.67: blind, eager and averse clauses differ in edge agreement by 40-73 SE at L=12 (stable from L=6), static differs about 7 times more, and N<|m|^2> is L-independent for blind and eager up to p=1000, so no ordered phase.
attack.price: Formation site choice is blind to the record state (single-site, exchangeable priorities): a reading of AX:40-41 plus AX:57, an owner decision, not derived.

title: The axioms contain no dynamics or action, and nothing selects one

members.title: The axioms contain no dynamics; every dynamics used is a supplied clause
members.plain: The axioms give odds at a site but no motion: no quantum state, no rule for how unrecorded things change, no clock, no rule that keeps a record once written. Every "dynamics" in this lane is an added sentence, in three separate families, and none is adopted. Records that form only from their neighbours can never reproduce quantum (Bell) correlations (they stay at CHSH 2); a supplied quantum sentence reaches 2.83.

members.title: No selection principle for the action, the Hamiltonian or the couplings
members.plain: Nothing in the axioms says which energy function or action governs the lattice, or even that it is nonzero. "No motion at all" fits every constraint proved so far, and the standard candidate actions (Wilson, heat-kernel, Manton) give measurably different answers at lattice scale. Every attempt to pick one has ended with the selection listed as still open. All couplings, stiffnesses and units are inputs.

members.title: Quantum kinematics (linear, completely positive, unitary, update) is derived only from supplied premises
members.plain: Ordinary quantum evolution (linear, reversible, sites combined as a product) is not in the axioms. It has been derived from side conditions such as 'far records cannot signal' and 'pure states stay pure and distinguishable'. Each derivation imports an extra premise, and the step that gives linearity imports the Born weights it is trying to explain.

attack.plain: The axioms give a site's odds but no law for how unrecorded parts of the lattice change in time, and nothing picks or even requires a nonzero one; that is true by design. The wall is equivalent to one named clause (a covariant Hermitian generator between records, records acting by compression, odds read by the trace rule), and this attack shrank it: given the trace-rule interface, the generator's nearest-neighbour range and its being nonzero follow from Admissibility, and under possibility covariance the only coupling left is a time unit that records cannot see. Records-only local rules cannot avoid the clause (Bell/CHSH), so it is priced, not passed.
attack.best_route: R1: derive the generator's range (cliques only) and nonvanishing from Admissibility locality plus 'varies with', given the landed trace-rule interface; missing obligation is an exact direction-only proof of the range lemma and the soldered family.
attack.test: Counted covariant local qubit generators by two independent methods (bond range 1 possibility-covariant / 3 soldered, matching the landed note; star range 24 / 692), showed NN-local isolated-site fields are exactly the clique (bond) subspace and, numerically, that no fine-tuned non-clique generator hides its far-record dependence (min far-dependence about 0.02 times the non-clique weight); thermal-time (modular flow) route gave operator-Schmidt rank 1, i.e. dead.
attack.price: The dynamics clause: between records unrecorded content evolves under a translation- and rotation-covariant Hermitian generator (D-dyn), records act by compression (D-perm), odds are read by the trace rule (D-tr); plus covariance flavour, a time unit, one preparation number c, and a joint-formation rule for adjacent unrecorded sites. Range and nonvanishing of the generator follow from Admissibility once D-tr is granted.

title: What a record is: a sharp birth costs bond energy, and a unitary Born wave cannot raise the record count

members.title: The wording of the dynamics depends on what a "record" is, and the simplest reading fails
members.plain: Which dynamics sentence is right depends on what a record is: a sharp one-site lock, a soft large-scale lock, a marker riding a quantum wave, or something that emerges. Tests so far kill the simplest picture: a sharp lock costs the energy of its bonds, and under a unitary wave a record count that never falls also never rises. No reading is derived from the axioms.

members.title: What a record is: every reading of "records form" has a price
members.plain: Something must turn quantum possibility into a permanent fact. A sharp one-site lock costs the energy of the site's bonds, gigajoules per record at the Planck scale. If records never disturb the wave, the wave is a second ingredient with non-local odds. Records that emerge by redundant copying scrambled instead of copying in the tests so far. Soft collapse needs a new length and rate. No reading is free.

members.title: "Records form" against a unitary wave with Born count statistics
members.plain: If the quantum wave evolves reversibly and the number of records follows Born statistics, the count cannot go up unless it can also go down. So 'records form from nothing and stay' contradicts a reversible wave. Escapes exist (irreversible collapse, non-Born counts, records as patterns, records that later die), but each is an added premise.

members.title: Records cannot be born by a unitary wave with Born count statistics
members.plain: Suppose the quantum wave evolves reversibly and the number of records follows the wave's odds. Then a count that never falls never rises, because a reversible rule that creates also destroys. Records could move but not appear. The owner's picture, where the count rises until the box freezes, therefore needs something outside this: a non-reversible step, count odds that are not the wave's, or records that can also die.

members.title: A sharp one-site birth costs the energy of its bonds, which heat budgets rule out
members.plain: If a record is a sharp lock of one site, it cuts that site's bonds. The energy is about 2 to 3.7 bond energies for Heisenberg qubits, or 2.4 hop energies for the walker sea. With the lattice tied to the speed of light, that is gigajoules per record at the Planck scale, and at 1e-19 m Earth's heat allows only about 2e-5 births per kg per second. Sharp births look unphysical at every spacing.

members.title: "Time is the creation of records" has no bridge to a clock and clashes with a unitary wave
members.plain: The owner's picture is that time is records being created or shifted. But if records ride on a unitary quantum wave with Born statistics, the record count cannot rise: records cannot form from nothing. And if a local clock rate is set by record events, Einstein's negative scalar mode either stays or an extra scalar graviton appears; closing it needs an indefinite kinetic form.

attack.plain: T03 is the bill for the quantum wave that Bell correlations force on the framework (T08): a record either cuts into the wave, which costs the bond energy it severs, or rides on it, which cannot raise a count. I checked that changing what 'form' means, the formation order, or the repository's second formation model does not remove the cost; each horn has exactly one exit (coherence-free bonds or a supplied record rest energy; a stored low-record source with horizon-limited permanence), and nothing makes records form from nothing at a sharp site.
attack.best_route: Records as arrivals from a stored low-record source (realized-state boundary) into a large reservoir: permanence horizon proportional to reservoir length, no collapse and no heat bill, but total number conserved.
attack.test: Exact cube, finite-rate GKLS law and Bell-process runs (T03_scratch): sharp lock 3.213 J is identical under update and refinement and order-independent; per-birth energy in the finite-rate law is exactly 0 or 2*Delta by convention; source route has no fall up to t~n (onset/n = 1.10, 1.05, 1.02) then 0.6 after recurrence; bulk formation rings show detailed balance and lifetimes of 6-12 hops.
attack.price: The dynamics-clause wave bought for Bell (T08), plus one exit per horn: coherence-free bonds or a supplied record rest energy (cost); a low-record stored source with horizon-limited 'permanent' (count).

title: Record identity: which record is which, and field flips versus permanence

members.title: Which record is which: identity and the beable are chosen, not derived
members.plain: In the moving-records picture a record hops between neighbouring sites, but the law that moves them moves unlabelled occupations. Whether 'the record' travels with a particle depends on a naming rule the dynamics does not fix. Following the record that hops, it stays home while the disturbance runs off. Naming by the wave's own bookkeeping makes it travel, but that changes with how the wave is written.

members.title: A field flip conflicts with permanent records unless records move with a fixed identity
members.plain: In the photon model a flip changes what a link holds, but the Record axiom says records are permanent. Read as records moving round a square, it needs a rule for which record is which. The rule is undefined so far, and different choices give different answers.

attack.plain: The wall says a moving record needs an identity rule and the rule changes the answers. For the photon flip that is misframed: two identical records go round a square with no tracking rule, and only their class (bosons, fermions, different contents) matters, changing the flip strength by 0.2 to 40 percent in the tested model and never to zero. A tagged record that lags a travelling disturbance is what the pattern picture predicts. The real price is different: record hops move a field only if the ice rule is soft (an exact rule freezes it), and hops leave readable records off their sites.
attack.best_route: R1: replace the identity rule by a distinguishability class (identical bosons, identical fermions, distinct contents) and compute the 4-hop ring flip; R3 (is the ice rule soft?) is the surviving replacement question.
attack.test: Exact 9-site window with two hard-core records, 7 parameter sets, two energy models: J_B = a1+a2 and |J_F| = |a1-a2| exactly, |J_F/J_B| between 0.60 and 0.998, never zero, exact diagonalisation within 2.3 percent of fourth order, leakage weight eps^2 = 2t^2/3 so J = 1.9 eps^4 Delta; 1D exact tracer check: the pre-registered density equality B1 FAILED (differs by up to 0.16, my error), tracer/excess ratio 0.28 to 0.36 as predicted (B2 passes).
attack.cheaper_question: With field-carrying records treated as one content class and a soft (finite-weight) ice rule, what are the ring coefficient, the many-plaquette exchange-sign structure and the leakage of readable records off their sites?

title: The statistical bridge (Born-type odds, odds to frequencies) is not derivable and is parked

members.title: The odds of a forming record are not supplied (the statistical bridge)
members.plain: The axioms say each forming record draws its content from a probability distribution set by its neighbours, but never say what that distribution is. Every route tried for deriving it from the lattice itself has been closed at the tested scope. The fallback is a new axiom, 'odds equal the action's normalised weights', which the owner parked: it must wait until the framework-level action is identified, and no plain-language sentence for it exists yet.

members.title: The statistical bridge (Born-type weights) cannot be derived and is parked unadopted
members.plain: Why should formation odds equal the weights the mathematics suggests (Born-type)? Every derivation door tried is closed at its stated scope: pure additivity cannot force it, no covariant dynamics can pick it, and the last live construction failed its own pre-set test. What is left is adopting it as a postulate. The text exists but is parked; the owner's rule is: identify the action first.

members.title: The record statistical bridge and the composition premise are unadopted
members.plain: The axioms give odds for which possibility a forming record locks. They give no odds or frequencies for whether and when records form, and no rule for how records combine. An earlier campaign proposed one postulate (formation odds equal normalized weights of the committed action). The owner parked it. So frequency language stays conditional, and the composition premise C-add is carried as a named premise.

members.title: The odds are not yet linked to long-run record frequencies
members.plain: The framework's odds say what a record locks when it forms. Nothing yet shows that counts of records in a long history follow those odds. Counts alone fix no probability law, and repeated records are not forced to be independent. One direct measurement found bulk-record frequencies differing from the weights by 0.05 to 0.12 in probability, stable in lattice size. The theory currently makes no frequency prediction.

attack.plain: The statistical bridge is three different things filed as one wall. The odds-form half is not statistical: for ordinary positive local odds a Born form comes free, so what is left is which action the odds come from (T02) and how an action becomes odds (T06). The frequency half is misframed: against the odds a record actually has given its recorded neighbours, frequencies are calibrated by a martingale fact with no clustering premise; what remains is the formation order (T01) and a universal typical-history rule.
attack.best_route: R1: prequential calibration lemma (martingale/Azuma) turns odds-to-frequencies into formation order (T01) plus content-independent formation plus a Cournot rule; first artifact is Lemma C with the finite-history scorer of the signing text as its test.
attack.test: Block-01 six-axis rule (3,1,2) on an open 4^3 window, 30000 histories per world, pre-registered: predictive odds are calibrated (chi2/df 1.37, 1.10) under random and value-dependent orders, static conditionals are calibrated in a heat-bath world (1.12), cross-pairings fail (13.7, 10.1), a content-dependent clock fails (5294 vs 1.06); exact cat/product arm obeys Var(F - mean predictive) <= 1/(4n); the Born-form parent Hamiltonian on the 2x2x2 cube is exact with gap 0.528; all pre-registered readings passed.
attack.cheaper_question: Which conditional are the axioms' odds (predictive along a formation order, or static), and does the signing text's finite-history calibration scorer separate them at about 10^4 records? What is left of the odds form is priced at T02/T06 (the action that fixes the amplitude).

title: Born trace-form conditions and the typed action-to-odds interface

members.title: The Born trace form needs menu-independence and menu abundance that the axioms do not give
members.plain: If a record's odds do not depend on which other outcomes are on offer, and the lattice offers enough different sets of outcomes, the Born rule is forced. Both conditions are extra. The axioms do not supply them, the lattice's own matter law offers too few outcome sets, and the constructed alphabet that offers enough needs further clauses (a scale-reading rule, continuity).

members.title: Which state the odds are read from: its purity and orientation
members.plain: Even granting the Born form, the lattice does not say which quantum state a forming record is read from. With the simplest local dynamics the state lines up with the field of the neighbouring records, but how sharply (ground state or thermal), and whether aligned or anti-aligned with the neighbour, is left open. The two signs give opposite correlations between adjacent records.

members.title: Even given an action, the axioms' odds are not identified with it (the typed interface)
members.plain: Suppose an action is chosen. The axioms' "odds" are still not automatically what the action calculates. An action gives a state; a state gives probabilities only after you say which question is asked; and the answer must be matched to what the record locks. Small exact examples show each link can fail separately. Owner options for wording this exist; none is adopted.

attack.plain: The axioms call the odds a probability measure on the possibilities. Read that way, the 'menu independence and menu abundance' list disappears (a menu just cuts one measure), and what is left is one condition: seen through yes/no readouts, the odds measure has only a dipole lean. That is the owner memo's two-clause primitive (pure-state certainty plus affinity read on readouts) reworded, so the wall is priced, not passed; W3's purity and sign are already priced in T02 and T23.
attack.best_route: R1 measure typing (Kochen-Specker/Bell template plus a hemispherical-transform lemma): Born on all hemisphere readouts iff the odd part of the odds density is exactly 2 r.u, the even part is free, positivity needs mean|f_odd|<=1; first artifact is that lemma with its runner, and the residual clause (pure-dipole odd part) is the price.
attack.test: hemi_test.py and hemi_test_E.py, pre-registered: hemisphere-transform eigenvalues match Funk-Hecke to 4.6e-10 (c_1=1/4, c_3=-1/16, even l>=2 zero); Kochen-Specker density 4t_+ gives cos^2(theta/2) to 1.1e-9 with pure dipole odd part; dipole-only densities cap Born purity at 1/2; Gibbs and power kernels are positive, covariant and certain but not Born; realisability criterion excludes the cubic witness (1.25>1) and admits the second (1.0); Wootters constant-Fisher scan over 15 laws selects only Born with purity 1; run 1 had five disclosed numeric FAILs, fixed; fixture-vs-thermal check inconclusive (0.0192 vs 0.02).
attack.price: The odds measure on the possibility sphere has a pure-dipole odd part (Born on every hemisphere readout), with certainty at pure endpoints: the owner memo's support calibration plus conditional affinity read on readout probabilities, i.e. the trace rule D-tr in measure form; plus the T02 preparation number and a T23-type sign.

title: Quantum equilibrium: why records start distributed as |psi|^2

members.title: Quantum equilibrium: why records start distributed as |psi|^2
members.plain: In the version where records ride on a wave, the wave keeps the Born statistics once records have them, but nothing makes records start with them. Out of that state the records could be used to send signals. The framework's realised-state primitive refuses any statement about typical starting states, so the usual fix is closed.

attack.plain: In the guided-records picture the wave keeps Born statistics but never creates them, so the records must start in them. Exact ensemble tests show the noise-free law does not wash out a wrong start: separated branches keep their weights, so CHSH ends anywhere from 0 to 3.5 and a two-site shift leaks a 16% signal, while an added equivariant noise of 7 to 10 hop rates does relax every start tried. Equilibrium therefore stays a premise, and it is unapproved rather than forbidden by the realized-state primitive.
attack.best_route: R2 (misframing): treat quantum equilibrium as the Born first-formation odds of the record configuration, a law-level clause at the T01+T05+T06 join that local formation can supply only if |psi_0|^2 is a Markov law; R1 with an equivariant noise clause is the alternative price.
attack.test: Exact ensemble master equation on the probe-5 Bell protocol (two rings of 24): equilibrium control 2e-15 and CHSH 2.791; five non-equilibrium starts end with CHSH 0.01 to 3.52 and a two-site shift leaks signal 0.158 at t=8; Metropolis noise gamma 7 to 10 restores CHSH 2.791 with signal <= 0.017; the kernel to t=8 forgets nothing (Dobrushin coefficient >= 1.0000).
attack.price: QE: the odds by which the record configuration is first formed, and before each branching, are the Born odds of the guiding wave (a law-level clause at the T01+T05+T06 join, needing a Markov |psi_0|^2); or alternatively N: an equivariant noise clause with rate about 7 to 10 hop rates. Neither follows from the four axioms or the realized-state primitive.

title: Records plus local odds cannot carry quantum (Bell) correlations

members.title: Records alone cannot carry quantum correlations; a wave with non-local odds is a second ingredient
members.plain: Records that form from neighbouring records alone behave like a local classical machine, so they cannot violate Bell's inequality: CHSH is at most 2, while quantum mechanics reaches 2.83. Reaching it needs a second ingredient, a wave over the not-yet-recorded sites, which the axioms lack. Bell's theorem then forces some non-local element into the odds.

members.title: Records alone cannot give quantum correlations; a wave with nonlocal odds is a second ingredient
members.plain: If records form locally and causally from records alone, their correlations cannot exceed the classical bound (CHSH 2), while quantum mechanics reaches 2.83. A wave over the records reproduces the quantum correlations, but then the odds for a record's next move depend on distant records, and the state is no longer just a configuration of records.

attack.plain: Records that form one at a time from neighbours cannot beat Bell's bound (CHSH at most 2), and the axioms alone do not say whether sites that form together may be correlated. An exact patch forming in one draw, with every single site's odds local, reaches CHSH 4 at any range, but only because a pair of middle records carries the far setting in its correlation; forbidding that (cluster locality) restores the bound. So the wall is exactly one premise, cluster locality, and passing it needs a wave or non-local formation units.
attack.best_route: Records as beables with a wave and Bell's jump law (probe 5, CHSH 2.79), the wave being shared with the propagation wall T09; co-formation reaches Bell only as a super-quantum overshoot that violates cluster no-signalling.
attack.test: Relaxation search over arbitrary nonnegative Gibbs-patch weights: chain with one middle site under single-site locality gave CHSH 2.0000 (900 starts); plaquette under single-site locality gave 4.0000 (293/300 feasible); plaquette under cluster locality gave 1.999993 (23/300 feasible); an exact-fraction 2-rail ladder gave CHSH 4 with all single-site marginals local and cut-pair total variation 1.
attack.price: CLUSTER-LOCALITY: no readable record cluster's joint statistics depend on a non-adjacent setting record, given Markov (nearest-neighbour) formation, exogenous settings and a single world; with it the CHSH bound is 2, without it a co-formed ladder reaches 4.

title: No propagation from records, odds or one-qubit ticks (waves need signed weights; no cone)

members.title: The record layer alone is diffusive: waves, inertia and 1/r fields need another layer
members.plain: Records governed by non-negative odds, like the axiom's distribution, spread out and settle. They do not oscillate. A wave needs signed amplitudes, and inertia or a long-range force needs a rule that is second order in time. So a record can be a source, with mass equal to the record count, but the field it makes has to live in an amplitude layer the axioms do not name.

members.title: The literal formation law does not propagate; the readings that do add a clause
members.plain: Read literally, each site gets one record once, with odds that cannot be negative. In the tested versions the laws this produces have the wrong character: irreversible, diffusive, effectively two-dimensional, no travelling waves and no three-dimensional potential. The readings that give waves or long-range order need a sentence the axioms exclude (records re-forming every tick), contradict (records that move), or lack (dynamics for the unrecorded amplitude).

members.title: A propagation cone does not come from records, odds or one-qubit ticks
members.plain: A light cone needs signals that travel at a finite speed. Odds-based rules (non-negative weights) can only spread out or slide rigidly; they cannot carry undamped waves. Simple one-qubit-per-site quantum ticks are either frozen or move at the top speed with no mass-like curvature. "Nearest neighbour" bounds how far a change could reach only once someone supplies an update rule.

members.title: Time: no master clock means no propagating field; discrete ticks are exact only for still walkers
members.plain: If no place has a master clock, a field of clock rates cannot carry a wave: the equations tie each place only to its neighbours and give no travelling mode. Adding a master clock fixes that but gives a speed set by the local rate and no sharp light cone. The lane's gravity-like law is therefore instantaneous (it acts at a distance). With discrete ticks a local clock rule stays exact only for walkers that do not move.

attack.plain: The wall is two walls: a finite-speed cone is free once any local update exists, and undamped waves need weights that can cancel, which non-negative odds cannot give (a non-negative unitary matrix is a permutation). A single qubit per site with one exact, rotation-symmetric, nearest-neighbour tick has no non-trivial unitary; the smallest carrier found that works is six-dimensional. With a Hamiltonian instead of a tick the qubit works, and covariance leaves only three free numbers, but the axioms supply neither.
attack.best_route: Supply a covariant nearest-neighbour Hermitian generator on the qubit-as-spinor (H = a + 2p sum cos k_i + 2q sum sigma_i sin k_i, 3 real numbers, continuous time); a strict single tick needs a carrier of dimension at least 6 (three qubits per site or one per link).
attack.test: Census of 55 exactly 24-fold-covariant radius-1 unitary ticks on Z^3 (integer reps to dim 6, spinorial to dim 8): none at s=2 (exact lemma for spin-1/2 x any taste); non-trivial only for the six-direction rep A1+E+T1 (cone speed 1/sqrt3), its sign twist, and spin-3/2 x taste2 (s=8); covariant Hermitian H on spin-1/2 has exactly 3 real parameters; non-negative and unitary coins meet only at permutations.
attack.price: AMPLITUDE-STEP: a nearest-neighbour update with negative or complex weights (cheapest form a covariant Hermitian generator on the qubit as spin-1/2, 3 real numbers; a strict tick needs carrier dimension >= 6), which the axioms explicitly do not supply (AX:116-123).

title: Pointer basis and redundant local observability are not derived

members.title: Pointer basis, context selection and local observability are not derived
members.plain: The axioms do not say which quantity a record registers, why it stays stable, or why many observers can read the same value. In the tests so far a bare site does not copy its bit into its surroundings, it scrambles it, and a pointer in a free sea gives a redundancy near 2 (the scrambled value), not 3. Objectivity needs structure the uniform lattice has not supplied.

members.title: Redundant readability of a record (local observability) is not derived
members.plain: The axioms make records permanent and readable only through records. They do not make a record readable by many independent observers, the 'copies everywhere' property that makes a fact objective. This has been an open gate since June. Tests on the lattice's own rules failed: a single site's bit scrambles into its surroundings instead of being copied.

attack.plain: Redundant readability is a property of the state, not a theorem of the law: on the same free-fermion lattice rule and the same pointer coupling, an equilibrium sea copies almost nothing at any size (1D up to 240 sites, 2D up to 16x16) while a stream of independent carriers gives redundancy that grows with the number of carriers. A covariant rule can also never single out one pointer axis, so the axis comes from the coupling or the state.
attack.best_route: R1/R3: replace 'derive redundancy from the axioms' by 'exhibit a law-admissible state with carrier flux', which needs a pointer-conserving switching coupling (dynamics, T02) plus registered realized-state data (T16); Gibbs-measure route R2 is wounded by kernel strength (T01) and Bell (T08).
attack.test: Exact Holevo information of local windows for pointer + free fermions (matches brute force to 4e-16): beam of N=1,2,3,4,6 carriers gives R(0.9)=2,2,4,4,>=7 (R(0.5)=2N); equilibrium sea gives R(0.9)=0, away windows <=0.15 bit (1D) and <=0.03 (2D); phase-only coupling gives <=0.008 bit; June star statistic is 4% at N=2 but 75% (R>=3) at N=12; pre-registered H5 (no 2-block invariant partition on 6/8/12 orbits) failed on the 8-vertex orbit, though no single axis exists.
attack.price: SWITCHING COUPLING + CARRIER FLUX: a pointer-conserving coupling that changes scattering probabilities (dynamics, sibling of T02) plus an incident many-carrier non-equilibrium state (registered realized-state data via realized_state_primitive, tied to T16); sufficiency checked for free fermions, necessity only suggested.

title: No bridge from records or ticks to a clock with a rate

members.title: No bridge from records or ticks to a clock with a rate
members.plain: The axioms say records form and stay, and nothing else about time. They do not say how fast, in what order, or how counting events becomes elapsed time. Every lane supplies its own clock. The natural identification, one tick equals one lattice step equals one unit of time, is a naming convention. Different clocks on the same rule give different physics, so the framework cannot yet say what "t" is.

members.title: Records give an order of events, not a rate: 'time is the creation of records' has no clock
members.plain: A record history tells you what came before what, and counts records. It does not give a rate. The owner's reading, 'time is the shifting or creation of records', would make local time the local event rate. But events that commute propagate nothing, and a rate needs a physical clock the record order does not supply. A frozen region would be a stopped clock, yet the gravity lane's clocks are assumed to tick.

attack.plain: The wall asks for a clock with a rate and a unit, but the unit is already a registered primitive and an overall rate is a relabelling that no record statistic can see. The two 2026-08-11 witnesses (formation probability 1/3 vs 2/3, parallel vs sequential completion) are one phenomenon, namely whether neighbouring sites may form at the same instant; once that is excluded, the only physical content is a probability measure on formation orders plus rate ratios between regions. That hands the residue to the formation-order wall T01 and the lapse question (T64/L14) and derives no clock.
attack.best_route: R1: treat formation events as a trace over the adjacency dependence graph (concurrency theory), so laws depend only on the acyclic orientation and Foata depth is a unit-free clock; it ends at an orientation measure, blocked-equivalent to T01.
attack.test: test_T11.py (exact/float, 6 graphs to the 8-site cube, plus a 12-ring hop chain): permutation classes = acyclic orientations (4,8,14,8,64,1862) with equal laws inside classes; parallel-kernel witness sits at L1 distance (3/5)q/(2-q) from the hull of ordered laws on two sites (0.225 at q=2/3 on the 7-site star) and tends to random-sequential as q->0; rate ratios change the final law, a common scale does not; once-only formation depth is 13.8 / 2 / 28 for i.i.d. / checkerboard / sweep orders at L=10; hops keep the Gibbs law on commuting layers (TV 1e-14) and lose it on simultaneous layers (TV 0.090).

title: Z^3 read as spacetime gives a 2D-skewed law or an excluded 3+1

members.title: The axioms' Z^3 gives a 2D-skewed spacetime or an excluded 3+1
members.plain: Records sit once on a 3D grid. If that grid is itself space plus time, only two dimensions are space, and the law comes out one-way and lopsided. To get three space dimensions plus time you must let records form again at every tick, which the axioms exclude, or add motion and waves from outside. The good results (long memory, an inverse-distance kernel) live on the excluded version.

attack.plain: If every grid site holds one record ever, the order among records has at most three dimensions whatever the rule, because an interval of chain-height h fits inside a ball of radius h on the grid and so holds at most about h^3 records where 3+1 needs h^4. The skewed 2D order is the best that layer can do and cube-symmetric growth orders do far worse. So 3+1 costs exactly one thing: each site must host a growing number of events, which the four axioms do not supply.
attack.best_route: R1: volume-height lemma (interval N <= (2h+1)(2h^2+2h+3)/3 for any site-once nearest-neighbour order) from causal-set counting, pricing 3+1 at events per site growing like h (moving records or amplitude updates with unrecorded inputs); necessity only, not a single round cone.
attack.test: interval_exponent.py on Z^3 event posets: every site-once sample obeys N <= ball(h) (max ratio 0.16); largest-interval exponent 2.83 for the level order, 1.32 and 1.01 for Eden growth from a point and a plane, iid times degenerate (chain 12), exact synchronous 3+1 lattice 3.87 and leaves the ball (ratio 2.13); random turnover top-third slopes 3.5-3.9 but two pre-registered readings (whole-range level fit, turnover exponent 3.6 with rising ratio) failed and were replaced by a disclosed top-third criterion.
attack.price: Unbounded events per site (events per site growing linearly with chain height): a persistence/update dynamics such as moving records or amplitude updates with unrecorded inputs, not in the four axioms (open gates MINIMAL_AXIOMS:183-185); re-recording every tick is the excluded case. Label: necessity argued (suggested, elementary proof) and checked numerically; sufficiency for one round cone belongs to T09/T11/T14.

title: Dimension and signature counts are declared (one time, odd time, three space)

members.title: Exactly one time (d_t <= 1) is a declared premise; the derivation routes tried are closed
members.plain: Nothing in the axioms says there is one clock rather than two independent ones. Two commuting clocks fit the axioms. Routes to exclude them either assume the answer, or cannot tell which lattice axis is time, because swapping time with a space axis is an exact symmetry of the staggered hop operator. The result is stated only conditional on a declared premise, B-AXIS.

members.title: An odd number of time dimensions rests on borrowed anomaly physics
members.plain: One argument says the number of time dimensions must be odd: a handed (chiral) particle needs an even total number of dimensions, and space is three. But it also assumes the standard anomaly rule, the Standard Model's charges and right-handed partners, none derived here. It yields 1, 3, 5, ..., not 1.

members.title: Three space dimensions are an axiom, not an output
members.plain: Why space has three dimensions is answered by the first axiom, not derived. The repository's attempt to select three from physics (attraction, stable orbits) works only among a short list of dimensions (1 to 5) and leans on imported physics criteria. Other results (the photon question, the generation count) lean on the number three.

attack.plain: Three space directions is an axiom, not a wall, and the 'odd number of times' argument is redundant once one time is shown. The real wall, 'exactly one time', is posed through a two-stopwatch witness that also exists inside an ordinary one-time chain, so it does not count times. Record permanence already gives a before-and-after order; if the emergent light cone is Lorentz-type, that forces exactly one time when space has three, which moves the wall to the cone-shape walls T14/T15.
attack.best_route: R2: permanence gives a pointed causal cone; an SO_0(p,q)-invariant pointed cone exists iff min(p,q)=1, so with d_s=3 it means d_t=1 (first artifact: record-order-to-cone bridge plus infrared covariance of that cone).
attack.test: Four scripts in T13_scratch: the N5 witness holds in a critical Ising chain (commutes with itself, fails to commute with the dynamics, 32 vs 0 when decoupled); local-charge census r<=6 gives 1 for a generic law and 2..11 for free laws; the cone lemma holds on 22 signatures; M_2(C) is Cl(3,0), Cl(1,2) and the even part of Cl(3,1)/Cl(1,3) only.
attack.cheaper_question: Does record permanence, extended to the emergent space, give a pointed causal cone that carries Lorentz-type covariance (time-orientation), rather than: how many independent commuting clocks exist?

title: One speed for every field is a premise and is not protected under interactions

members.title: One speed for every field is a registered primitive, not a derivation
members.plain: Space and time could be stretched differently on the lattice, so different fields could travel at different speeds. The framework fixes this by adopting, as an approved building block, that one tick equals one edge in form. Every attempt to derive that from the other axioms is circular or fails. The gravity member is not covered by the block, and on the campaign's continuous-time surface its speed is a free number.

members.title: One cone is not protected under interactions on the campaign's own time
members.plain: Even if two fields start at the same speed, interactions shift each one's speed by a different amount, and the shift does not vanish as the lattice is refined. Experiments limit such differences to about one part in 10^15 or better (an external figure quoted in the probe note). A symmetry can prevent it, but the symmetry that works is not the one the campaign's dynamics uses.

members.title: The photon and matter need one light cone, and nothing forces it
members.plain: For relativity the photon and the fermions must travel at the same top speed. The approved primitive says the time tick is one lattice edge for matter, but it does not say this for the photon's field. In a tested toy (a walker plus a scalar with a Yukawa coupling) the two speeds drift apart by 0.026 g^2, and the gap does not shrink as the lattice is refined.

members.title: The graviton's speed must equal the matter light speed, and only an added premise protects it
members.plain: Light and gravity waves must travel at the same speed to about one part in 10¹⁵. In the lattice comparator the speeds of two coupled fields drift apart at second order, by an amount that does not shrink as the grid gets finer. An added rule (a tick counts like a space step) protects them; it is approved for matter but not for the gravity field.

attack.plain: Fields on the grid can start at one top speed, but interaction nudges each by a different amount that does not vanish as the grid is refined. A symmetry prevents it: one tick of time counts as exactly one grid step, registered for matter only. This attack shows the gap is exactly zero at equality, turns on linearly with any mismatch, and that the 'speeds attract each other' escape is about 65 times too slow at electromagnetic strength.
attack.best_route: R1: read the primitive's regulator-block clause as defining every field's Euclidean action on the hypercubic block (real time H = -ln T/a); reduces the wall to that owner ruling plus T15.
attack.test: One-loop Yukawa (naive Dirac + scalar) on a Euclidean lattice with time step eps: speed gap is 0 to 1e-16 at eps=1, 1.5e-3/2.05e-2/5.9e-2 g^2 at eps=0.9/0.5/0.05 (reaching probe 3's continuous-time value; fermion piece matches to 1-2%), slope 0.008-0.08 g^2 per unit mismatch, attractor exponent 0.107 g^2 (about 0.0098 at alpha=1/137, needs 0.65).
attack.price: P*: every field's Euclidean kinetic form and interaction sit on the hypercubic Z^3 x Z_tau block with a_tau = a_s exactly (the kinetic_isotropy_primitive's regulator-block clause extended from matter to the gauge and spin-2 member actions), plus T15 (Euclidean protection carries to real time).

title: The Euclidean tick that protects the cone is not the real-time step (and sets the exponent 16)

members.title: The Euclidean tick that protects the cone is not the real-time step of the dynamics
members.plain: The symmetry that protects the cone is a statement about a Euclidean lattice with four equal directions. The framework's dynamics runs in real time. The continuation between the two is proved only for small free systems, and at finite spacing they give different energies. Choosing one changes a headline number (the hierarchy exponent, 16 versus 8), and the tick that keeps a cone cannot carry a one-handed particle.

members.title: Why the exponent is 16 (Euclidean fourth direction and regulator choice, gate B3b / P2)
members.plain: The "sixteen" exists only if time is treated as a fourth space-like lattice direction, a Euclidean device. With real-time evolution (the lane's own single-clock theorem), the count is eight and the formula lands near 5e10 GeV, not 246. Other equally standard lattice fermions have one, two or four copies. The notes call sixteen imposed by the regulator choice, not derived.

attack.plain: The grid tick that protects the light cone is not a real-time step, but nothing needs it to be: lattice theory defines real time as the continuous flow of the Hamiltonian read off the Euclidean transfer matrix, and a real-time step at equal edges is unstable in two or three space dimensions anyway. The count 16 is not Euclidean-only: for free fermions the real-time space rebuilt from the Euclidean staggered block is exactly two copies of the Hamiltonian one, so 16 versus 8 is a choice of matter regulator (one copy or two), not of time. The wall reduces to a named premise plus the missing interacting action (T02).
attack.best_route: Route A: define real time as the OS flow of the positive two-step transfer matrix (Luscher 1977; Sharatchandra-Thun-Weisz 1981); first artifact is the exact identity |det D| = 2^(-nL) Z_KS(+-asinh r)^2, checked to 1.7e-13 on free staggered blocks (d=1-3).
attack.test: Exact free staggered determinants on N^d x L blocks (23 cases) match two Hamiltonian copies with dispersion asinh(r) to 1.7e-13 while one copy misses by 0.12-88; the equal-edge real-time leapfrog is unstable on 0 / 50 / 79 percent of the zone for d=1 / 2 / 3 (massless) and stable exactly for tau <= 1/sqrt(d); one-step unitary ticks have 8 nodes and no quasi-energy-pi corner.
attack.price: The physical matter space is the unrooted OS reconstruction of the hypercubic staggered block on Z^3 x Z_tau (kinetic-isotropy primitive + staggered-Dirac gate + reflection positivity of the interacting action + no rooting), with real time its continuous flow; N is the mode count of that space (16 unrooted staggered, 8 Kogut-Susskind). Checked for free fermions, suggested for the interacting case.

title: The arrow of time needs a low-record past

members.title: The arrow of time needs a low-record past
members.plain: Records give the arrow its direction, away from the state with fewest records. But the framework does not supply that starting state, and its equations run equally well backwards. Start from a high-record state and the arrow reverses. 'Begin with few records' is an extra input, the same as physics' past hypothesis. Closed reversible rules cannot prepare a blank starting register either.

members.title: The arrow of time needs a low-record start
members.plain: Record formation gives time its direction: away from a start with few records. Why the world began with few records is not derived. The one reduction achieved holds only if records form a single chain, and it leaves the thermodynamic question (why so little entropy) untouched.

members.title: The uniform, low-disorder start (past hypothesis, homogeneity, no heat added later) is handed in
members.plain: Cosmology needs a very special beginning: nearly uniform, low disorder, and no extra heat injected later. The axioms only say a state is a set of records and that the law favours no state. So the special start, and the uniformity of the sky, must be supplied. The lane names this and prices it as an input; nobody has tried the horizon problem.

attack.plain: The wall mixes four questions. The record arrow (later means more records) already follows from permanence for every history, and since 2026-07-04 the axiom 'Records form' removes the empty-history escape the entry cites; the June 'reversal' comes from a unitary toy whose records its own second pass erases. What is left is whether matter's arrow follows record births (T03's fork) plus a first state and a random-order formation measure (T01).
attack.best_route: Ask whether record births act on the matter wave (T03 horn 1) instead of why the past was low; the symmetric-blank reading (R1) prices the boundary at zero bits but needs T01's random-order measure.
attack.test: Four scripts: June toy's second pass erases its records; 6-ring: empty is the only symmetric configuration but the symmetry-loss Lyapunov failed (79,596 of 605,052 births raise symmetry); 2D growth: symmetric start homogeneous, 4 seeds not (plateau 1.63/1.08 vs 8.91); 8 qubits: passive births keep start-dependent alignment (dS +1.47 Neel, -1.47 reversed), active locks drive energy toward equilibrium from every start.
attack.cheaper_question: Which arrow is asked for? Record inclusion is settled by permanence. For matter: do record births act on the wave (T03 horn 1: energy runs toward equilibrium from any start, at T03's bond-energy price) or not (the wave needs its own far-from-equilibrium start)? Remaining named residuals: a first state (or past-infinite growth) and a random-order formation measure (T01).

title: One record per site breaks the exact energy-momentum books of interacting matter

members.title: One record per site breaks the exact conservation books and leaves the exchange sign open
members.plain: Letting a site hold at most one record turns records into an interacting gas. For free walkers that can share a site, energy and momentum are exactly conserved and the gravity route works. With hard-core exclusion the conservation fails at third order and no local fix restores it. The axioms also do not say whether swapping two identical records gives a plus or a minus.

members.title: One record per site is an interaction that breaks the energy and momentum books; three things cannot all hold
members.plain: Matter is supposed to source gravity through exact bookkeeping (energy and momentum in equal out). That works for free particles. When particles obey "one record per site" they lose the bookkeeping at leading orders and nothing local restores it; the price of forming a record is not local either. Three things cannot all hold: the chosen gravity field, one-per-site records, and exact equations.

members.title: Lattice matter has no exact local stress-energy books (momentum, angular momentum) once it interacts or excludes
members.plain: A graviton can couple consistently, and stay massless, only to matter whose energy and momentum are conserved exactly at each place. Lattice matter conserves energy locally but generally not momentum. Under the one-record-per-site rule or with scattering, the bookkeeping fails at third order or entirely, and angular momentum cannot be kept with momentum on six axes unless records never scatter.

attack.plain: Exact bookkeeping of energy, momentum and turning-momentum fails for interacting Hamiltonian walkers because their momentum is a Fourier variable on a torus, not a local conserved label; hard-core exclusion is only one of the interactions that does it. For records whose momentum is an additive label (the moving-records clause), the lane's 'they can never scatter' conclusion holds only for neighbouring pairs: diagonal-pair and plaquette scattering keeps number, momentum and angular momentum exactly with one record per site.
attack.best_route: R1: classical moving-records clause V* (perpendicular neighbours wait, converging records swap contents, plaquette-local scattering); first artifact: couple the curvature member to V* and test its Gauss law on one event.
attack.test: Exhaustive cluster census plus exact symmetric-stress solves (2D and 3D) found P- and L-preserving non-bond scattering with a compact symmetric stress; torus ergodicity check needed an amended Lz mod 4 label (pre-registered reading failed); exact local-charge census of the two-record walk gave 0 odd charges for excluded and soft-interacting pairs in 2D (free controls 12 scalar, 16 walker).
attack.price: F: record momentum is the Fourier (Brillouin-torus) momentum of a Hamiltonian walker, together with local interaction and exact Gauss laws E for the member; exits are label momentum (classical clause, with costs), dropping E (pay the T61 shape/mass tuning, about 1e-102 in graviton mass squared, a reading), or non-scattering matter.

title: The exchange sign: nothing forces fermions over hard-core bosons

members.title: The exchange sign: nothing forces fermions over hard-core bosons
members.plain: The axioms make each site a two-state qubit and allow one record per site. That fits fermions, and equally well "hard-core bosons": identical at one site, but different when two are swapped in two or three dimensions. Every route tried to force the fermion sign has failed. The one theorem that gets it assumes a fermionic (Grassmann) measure at the start.

members.title: The exchange sign (statistics) is not supplied by records
members.plain: Do swapped identical records pick up a minus sign (fermions) or not? Both choices satisfy every axiom exactly. They first differ in a fourth-order energy moment, and for the reduced walk their spectra coincide on odd rings. So matter statistics must be supplied from outside.

members.title: Relativity and positivity for the lattice fermion: the standard spin-statistics route is only partly built
members.plain: The textbook proof that spin-1/2 goes with fermion statistics needs relativity, positive energy and causality. The lattice supplies none of these exactly. The reconstruction that would produce them from the lattice has been built for the free case only, in two of three pieces, with named gaps, and depends on supporting notes that are not ratified.

members.title: Reflection positivity of the Kahler-Dirac fermion on non-uniform (curved) histories
members.plain: Fifty-three notes dated 14 August to 5 September tried to show that the staggered fermion stays a proper positive quantum theory when the lattice cells are non-uniform. Every finite test returned a table with no positive-definite pairing, and no general theorem was reached in either direction.

attack.plain: Swapping two identical records either gives a minus sign (fermions) or not (hard-core bosons), and the four axioms allow both. Read as nearest-neighbour rules on unlabelled records, though, no rule of bounded reach can give far-apart records the minus sign in two or three dimensions; the fermion sign needs a string of unbounded reach. So the sign is not a free bit: fermions cost a named non-local (graded) clause, and locality alone tilts toward bosons.
attack.best_route: R1: state GL(F) as the negation of amplitude-level bounded-range locality for the sign (plus a grading); fallback R2, an emergent fermion from an entangled vacuum, first artifact the T-junction phase in the Wen plaquette model on Z^2.
attack.test: Exact F_2 linear algebra over all diagonal gauges and all bounded-range sign rules: smallest solving range r*(L)=L-1 for 2D N=2 (L=3..8) and 3D (L=2..4), r*=0 in 1D; coin-walker exchange loops on nine rings have X_f=-X_b with different spectra, so no gauge maps the fermion sector to a bounded-range rule.
attack.price: GL(F): graded (string-carrying) composition of records, equivalent to dropping bounded-range amplitude locality (AMP-LOC) for the exchange sign in d>=2, plus a choice of grading of M_2(C).

title: A local fermion on one qubit per site: the string / extra-qubit trilemma

members.title: Local fermions on one qubit per site: the string / extra-qubit trilemma
members.plain: With one qubit per site, a fermion hopping between neighbours in 2D or 3D needs a long chain of extra operations across the lattice (a Jordan-Wigner string). Local codes exist, but they put qubits on links, add constraints, and are not selected by the axioms. So "fermionic", "local" and "one qubit per site" have not been shown to hold together.

members.title: What is the fermion's local space? Mode, spin coin, or half a composite
members.plain: Different parts of the lane use the one qubit in incompatible ways: as one fermion mode (the June gate), as the two-component spin "coin" of a walker (September campaign, which also needs four states per site once occupation counts), or as half of a two-qubit composite (Kitaev-style networks). The axioms do not say which. The owner's "particles are patterns of records" reading suggests none is the fermion.

members.title: Composition of sites: the joint state space is supplied
members.plain: Entanglement needs the joint state space of two sites to be the tensor product of their one-site spaces. Locality alone does not force that. The repo obtains it from two supplied admissions or from local tomography. The only alternative tested, a fermion comparator with parity superselection, fails local tomography.

attack.plain: A fermion on one qubit per site with only nearby operations is impossible in 2D or 3D if you want an exact encoding on the whole space (checked at Pauli level: the needed operator range grows with lattice width, and spare qubits without constraints do not help). Local encodings do exist, but they need extra qubits plus constraints, and their vacuum is a topologically ordered (toric-code-like) state. On Z^3 the extra qubits are just other sites, so 'one qubit per site' survives literally, at fermion density 1/8 with a period-2 role pattern and a chosen sector.
attack.best_route: R1: BKSF-type code on the cubic cell complex embedded in Z^3 (roles by coordinate parity); first artifact is a translation/rotation-covariant nearest-neighbour rule that produces the 8-class role pattern and the flat sector.
attack.test: Exact SAT on grids: 1D encodes at range 0; 2D range r*=floor(W/2) for widths up to 5 and 6x6 fails at r=2 (all SAT models re-verified); BKSF vacuum on 2D/3D tori has 4/8 locally indistinguishable states like the toric code; Z^3 site graph equals cubic-complex incidence with vertex density 1/8.
attack.price: CODE-SECTOR: matter lives in the constrained subspace of a supplied local gauge-type code (role pattern plus flat sector), given ungraded tensor composition; the other price is graded composition (T18).

title: Spin-1/2 and the Dirac law are supplied

members.title: Spin-1/2: how a rotation acts on the qubit is a choice, not a consequence
members.plain: The axioms give the lattice cube rotations and give each site a qubit, but do not say how a rotation acts on the qubit. Four inequivalent ways fit. Calling the qubit spin-1/2 in the physical sense (turn by 360 degrees, get a minus sign) is a further choice: a spin-blind action satisfies every constraint and gives identical numbers.

members.title: The Dirac law itself: kinetic law, one flux bit, holonomy and time are supplied
members.plain: The axioms give no motion law. A qubit lattice can just as well move qubits by neighbour swaps, an ordinary slow non-relativistic law with one zero of the dispersion, as by the relativistic Dirac law with eight zeros. The Dirac choice is currently made by adding a class of laws, one sign bit (picked by a thermal requirement), a boundary convention and a time direction.

attack.plain: The lane's separate premises (faithful spin-1/2 lift, kinetic class, flux bit, boundary convention) collapse, for a nearest-neighbour walker whose coin is the site qubit, into one: the cube's rotations turn the qubit's Bloch vector the way they turn space (full soldering). Given it, the double cover is forced by finite-group theory and the covariant nearest-neighbour law is fixed up to three numbers: a Weyl law with eight linear cones (4 right, 4 left). Full soldering itself, the walker and the dynamics clause are still supplied, so the wall is priced, not passed.
attack.best_route: R1: classify covariant nearest-neighbour laws per soldering action (done, survives as a reduction); further step R3: show the Admissibility 'varies with' sentence plus order-blind positive formation forces trivial kernel, i.e. full soldering (lemma stated, not run; wounded since order-blindness is supplied).
attack.test: Runners test_A..E: only full soldering has no linear 2-dim lift of the cubic group (-1 in [2O,2O]); covariant nearest-neighbour laws have dimension 8/4/3/3 and only full soldering gives isolated cones (H = e0 + e1 sum cos k + a sigma.sin k, eight cones, charge +-1, 4 right and 4 left); at range 1 and 2 the Gamma cone is a*identity only for full soldering; nearest-neighbour covariant ticks are pure phases; 311 of 400 random non-covariant laws have anisotropic charge +-1 cones.
attack.price: SOLDER-T1: full soldering of the proper cubic rotations on the qubit (Bloch vector rotates as the lattice vector), together with the walker (site qubit as one-particle coin) and a nonzero nearest-neighbour first-order clause (a != 0); the strong reading of 'no possibility is privileged' must be rejected.

title: Rest energy (mass) has no source in the rules

members.title: A Dirac mass: rest energy has no source in the rules
members.plain: A massless lattice walker is a supplied model. Giving it a rest energy needs an extra alternating term (a staggered mass) that nothing in the covariant rules produces. Attempts that derive one need a coupling tuned below a threshold, or a supplied time-reversal-odd term, and often give a rest energy of lattice size.

members.title: No rest energy (mass) is induced; it is supplied
members.plain: The lane's basic moving particle has no rest mass: the qubit space has no room for a term that would give it one (checked). Mass needs an added staggered term, or binding of two particles; binding works in one dimension but is killed by "one record per site" and is lopsided in three. Rest mass is supplied, not derived.

attack.plain: A walker's rest energy needs a background that alternates from site to site like a chessboard, and no translation-invariant term can supply it. The lane's price for making that chessboard from records (bond factor below 1.4e-4) is a proof bound: the record gas is exactly the 3D Ising antiferromagnet and orders below g of about 0.41, and the walker keeps a band-edge gap there with localized defect levels. But the chessboard exists only if records equilibrate; random permanent formation orders leave no clean gap, so the mass now rests on an equilibrating formation law, g < 0.41 and a free scalar coupling c that sets the scale.
attack.best_route: R1: record-gas Neel phase (3D Ising antiferromagnet, g < 0.412) coupled to the walker as c*n_x; needs the hidden premise EQUIL (records equilibrate despite permanence) and a free c
attack.test: Ran gas-Ising identity (exact), Wolff MC Binder crossing (g_c ~ 0.41), walker spectra with IPR on Gibbs samples (band-edge gap survives at g=0.25, L=8,10; halves at g=0.35), formation-order contrast (lexicographic exact chessboard; random permanent orders leave 4-8x more in-gap states), mean-field CDW V_c=0.366
attack.price: STAGGERED-ORDER: a chessboard record background from an equilibrated Neel-phase gas (g < 0.412, ensemble supplied) plus a scalar walker coupling c (m = c<sigma>/2, c free)

title: Chirality: every free local walker has a mirror twin; the chiral weak SU(2) is added

members.title: Chirality: every free local walker has a mirror twin, and a qubit has no left/right switch
members.plain: The weak force treats left- and right-handed matter differently. Every simple free lattice walker comes with a mirror twin of opposite handedness: proved for the campaign's walker (4 right + 4 left) and for any strictly local tick. A single qubit has no left/right switch either. Nothing in the framework yet makes matter chiral.

members.title: The chiral weak SU(2) and anomaly-complete hypercharge are added by premises
members.plain: The weak force acts only on left-handed particles. Here the su(2) comes from the same Clifford algebra as spin, and nothing makes it a left-handed gauge field. The right-handed partners and the anomaly-free hypercharge come from extra premises. The hypercharge pattern (+1/3, -1) is a left-handed eigenvalue pattern whose overall scale is set by hand.

attack.plain: A simple lattice walker always comes with a mirror twin of opposite handedness, and a weak force acting on left-handed matter only is the same obstruction, because any internal symmetry of such a walker treats both handednesses alike. Every way out (interactions that gap the twins, a non-finite-range update, an extra dimension) also needs the full anomaly-free 15/16-state family of matter, which the framework's native 8-state surface lacks, and 30-32 lattice nodes against the 8 or 16 supplied. The update-with-tails way out now has a checked price: it pumps the tick phase in parallel electric and magnetic fields.
attack.best_route: Symmetric mass generation on the completed 16-plet (32 nodes); first artifact is the SPIN10 note's open obligation N6, a finite-coupling chiral phase with a cone-counting current spectrum.
attack.test: Three same-family checks: 40 random SU(2)-symmetric walkers all have zero chirality per isotype; the anomaly ledger gives SU(3)^3=2, Y^3=-16/9 for the native 8-state surface and a unique 7-state completion (SM), 15 vs 16 states; the range-2 tails tick on a 12x12 flux torus has determinant winding +48 = 4*N_phi while strictly local ticks give 0.

title: The orientation (handedness) bit is not fixed

members.title: Which hand: the orientation bit is not fixed by anything
members.plain: Even if the framework produced a chiral rule, nothing says which hand nature has. The axioms name only proper rotations and are silent on reflections, so a handed law needs one extra yes/no datum. The arrow of time does not fix it. The owner has parked the question, with the standing default that neither reading is adopted.

members.title: Symmetry breaking S3 to C3 and the handedness choice
members.plain: If the lattice's full axis-permutation symmetry were exact, the three leptons could have only two different masses. Three distinct masses need that symmetry cut down to cyclic rotations, and the cut has been traced to one yes/no handedness choice. The same choice fixes which sign of the phase is physical. No derivation forces that handedness; the owner has parked the question.

members.title: One unsupplied orientation bit sits under both halves of theta-bar
members.plain: A twist angle needs a sense of handedness: which way is right-handed, and which way records are ordered. The axioms supply rotations but not mirror reflections, so they do not say whether the law can tell left from right. Mirror-asymmetric rules are allowed. The same missing bit sits under the mass half, because flipping handedness is complex conjugation on the qubit algebra. The real weak force is handed, so "the law is mirror-symmetric" cannot simply be assumed.

attack.plain: The wall bundles different yes/no labels. The flavor one (S3 to C3, sign of the Brannen phase) is not a left/right choice: the lattice's own proper rotations flip it, so it is a direction along a cube diagonal and its absolute sign is a convention; only signs relative between sectors can matter. What is left is the parked reflection decision behind the strong-CP and weak-sector members, which points the opposite way (blind law versus handed law), and a state-level question of which rotation and translation symmetry the realized state breaks.
attack.best_route: Replace 'derive the hand' by 'which subgroup of proper rotations and translations does the realized state preserve, is any reflection-odd term present, and which cross-sector orientation products are invariant' (R1); the outside route (symmetric law, broken state, Nelson-Barr texture) is blocked-equivalent to T43.

title: Doublers: eight or sixteen copies with no rule to keep or remove them

members.title: Doublers: eight (or sixteen) copies, protected by symmetry, with no rule to keep or remove them
members.plain: A lattice fermion of this kind comes with 8 copies in space (16 if time is also a lattice). The framework declines to remove them (it treats the lattice as physical), so they must be real particles. Nothing says which are which, what would lift them, or why the count matches nature. The walker's own symmetries keep them in exactly degenerate pairs.

attack.plain: Keeping the copies is not a missing rule: if the qubit turns as a spinor under two perpendicular half-turns, or a time reversal squares to -1, the eight band touchings are forced at every range, so the count is a fact about the symmetry class. Removing them means breaking both symmetries (one pair at best, no three-generation triplet), and a chessboard-ordered state can lift copies only in balanced pairs, never the mirror triplet alone. Also, '8 or 16' counts unlike objects.
attack.best_route: R1: state the count as a symmetry-class theorem (non-abelian corner stabiliser: weak SOLDER-T1 of T20, or Kramers) and price removal as its loss; first artifact tests A1-A4 (run); the interacting escape for the mirror stays with T22.
attack.test: Random covariant two-band rules (600 per group, ranges 1-3): all 8 corner touchings pinned to 1.1e-14 under O, D4 and D2 (two perpendicular half-turns), unpinned in 100% under C4z, C2z or no group; explicit two-node rule breaks D2 and Theta; exact 8^3 torus diagonalisation of a period-2 term gives zero-mode counts 16/12/4/0 with E^2=|sin k|^2+m^2; linearised corner-mass classification never leaves the hw=1 triplet alone with a gapped remainder; zero-mode census gives 8, 4, 16, 16 Weyl nodes for walker, Kawamoto-Smit, naive 4-component, ordered tick.

title: Matter content and species labels (SM table, taste cube, dark sector host) are supplied

members.title: Species labeling (AC_phi_lambda): which corner is which particle
members.plain: The three equal-looking corner states (the hw=1 triplet) are exchanged by a lattice rotation. members.plain: The masses come from a 3x3 matrix on the three cube-corner states. members.title: The quarks themselves (content, colour, charges, Higgs, family labels) are supplied, not derived
members.plain: The four axioms speak of a lattice, a two-state system per site, a local rule and permanent records. They say nothing about quarks, colour, electric charge, a Higgs, or which family is which. Every quark and CKM result starts from a Standard Model table put in by hand, so the lane can only say "if quarks look like this, then...". members.plain: Every neutrino result assumes objects the axioms do not contain: chiral fermions, a neutral right-handed neutrino, three generations, Higgs doublets and gauge couplings. All 326 neutrino/PMNS rows in the audit ledger are unaudited, and none of 131 lane notes cites the current axiom memo.

members.title: The axioms supply no dark sector, and the "taste cube" that would host one is an unclosed bridge
members.plain: The four axioms say nothing about what dark matter is. The dark-matter notes borrow a larger structure, a cube of eight "taste" states meant to carry Standard Model charges, and call two of the eight dark. The bridge from the axioms to that cube is itself on the axiom memo's list of open gates. So the framework has no derived answer yet to "what is dark matter".

The last cannot share the taste cube: on the repo's own embedding the three generation states carry different electric charges, and the walker supplies 8 Weyl points where three generations need 48. So the price is a second, product carrier (gauge content x flavour 3), not one table plus a convention.

title: The gauge group and the colour carrier are not selected from the carrier

members.title: The gauge group is not selected from the carrier
members.plain: The axioms give each site one qubit, so the only symmetry they hand over is that qubit's su(2). The repo builds a six-state block (3 colours x 2 weak states) to reach SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1). On that block the algebra fits the far larger U(6) equally well. Choosing the product subgroup as "the forces" needs a rule the axioms do not contain.

members.title: The colour carrier (MR_color) is not derived
members.plain: A bond of two qubits naturally holds a 3-dimensional block plus a 1-dimensional block, and su(3) acts on the 3-block. Nothing yet says quarks live in that block, that readable records are colour-neutral, or that the colour index rides on the links. Three separate bridges are missing, and the July campaign split them into eight named premises.

attack.plain: The lane's own suggested test fails: the hopping on the taste cube has no non-abelian symmetry, so it cannot select the gauge algebra. The lattice's own translations also move the graph-first colour su(3); the smallest translation-closed algebra containing it is su(4)+su(2) (dim 18), and with axis permutations su(8). So the Standard Model algebra needs a covariant parent gauging plus a chosen vacuum, a higher price than the three premises the lane recorded.
attack.best_route: R2: take the lattice-covariant parent (su(4)+su(2) or su(8)) and get su(3)+su(2)+u(1) as the isotropy of a vacuum (Wen PSG/IGG, Landau-Michel); first artifact is an order parameter with that isotropy, which is not yet derived (wounded).

attack.price: GAUGING-COV: a lattice-covariant gauge algebra on the taste cube (dim at least 18, su(4)+su(2), or su(8) with full cubic covariance) together with a vacuum whose isotropy is su(3)+su(2)+u(1); equivalently the choice of link group (gauging principle).

title: Non-abelian gauge links have no account in one-qubit-per-site records

members.title: Non-Abelian gauge links have no account in one-qubit-per-site records
members.plain: A force-carrying link for SU(2) needs at least four states (two qubits), and one for SU(3) at least six (three qubits). When one is built, the readable pattern of which state each site holds cannot even represent a colour-neutral state in the tested model: none of 65,536 patterns satisfies the non-Abelian Gauss law. Readable content sees colour only through singlets.

attack.plain: The wall mixes a storage cost (an SU(N) link needs 2N states, so more than one qubit) with a readout artifact (no colour-labelled pattern is colour-neutral) and a real gap (nothing forms multi-site links). Reading the wall's own model through colour-blind local labels, the non-abelian Gauss law becomes a local parity rule on record patterns and the dynamics stays local, so colour is not invisible; what remains is forming and hosting those label registers.
attack.best_route: R1: use colour-blind local labels (matter count, link orientation, one local pair-Casimir label at busy vertices) as the records; the Gauss law is then a Z_N centre-parity star constraint, which reduces T27 to T77, T10 and register hosting.
attack.test: Five finite scripts on the wall's own SU(2) model plus star, valence-6 and SU(3) vertices: baseline reproduced (0/65536 patterns, 82 singlets, E0=-sqrt34); all 1296 atoms have Gauss rank 0 or 1 and the 82 rank-1 atoms are exactly the parity-rule atoms; hop is single-link local; on a 4-link star 64 atoms have rank 2 and one local pair Casimir resolves them; all passed.

title: The gauge action and g_bare = 1 (beta = 6) are supplied

members.title: The gauge action and its normalization (g_bare = 1, beta = 6) are supplied
members.plain: The axioms say they are not a dynamics axiom, and list "g_bare = 1 convention handling" as an open gate. The repo sets the strong coupling to exactly 1 (beta = 6) by two conditional identifications. One matches the Wilson action's coefficient to a target. The other says a "slot" fixed by rigidity is the coupling. The action's form is also assumed.

members.title: g_bare = 1 (beta = 6): convention or input, and the two identifications behind it
members.plain: Every coupling in the chain starts from "the bare gauge coupling is 1", meaning the lattice gauge action has strength beta = 6. The repo calls this a harmless convention in one place and an open gate in another. The algebra shows only that g and beta are two names for one number. Fixing the number needs two undemonstrated identifications. It is not harmless: the weak-scale formula goes as its 32nd power.

attack.plain: The axioms never say how strongly a link fluctuates from one tick to the next, and 'g_bare = 1' (beta = 6) is that strength set to one radian per tick. Given the repo's dictionary, its second identification (SLOT-ID) is just 'beta = 6' restated, and the 'harmless convention' reading fails on the repo's own premises. Reading the strength off the exact transfer operator, the repo's named next route, gives beta about 6.8-7.6, not 6, so the number is a leading-order statement that needs one free rate per tick.

title: No controlled bridge from the Planck lattice to physical scales (transmutation, 17 decades)

members.title: The bridge from the Planck lattice to the physical strong coupling is missing
members.plain: The lattice coupling is set at the lattice scale. The repo reads it as the strong coupling at 246 GeV, then runs it to M_Z with standard QCD. Run instead from the lattice scale, an ordinary coupling of this size hits infinity far above 246 GeV. A beta = 6 lattice with spacing at the Planck scale would confine near 10^18 GeV, not 0.2 GeV. The 0.1182 match depends on two declared choices.

members.title: From the cutoff scale to the observed scales: Lambda_QCD << 1/a and the coupling transport
members.plain: Put a strongly coupled force theory on a Planck-size lattice and all its own scales sit near the Planck scale. The strong-force scale we observe is about 6 x 10^18 times lower. The repo bridges the gap by declaring the lattice coupling to be the coupling at 246 GeV, and by a formula for the weak scale with open pieces. Ordinary running from the lattice value blows up far above 246 GeV. No note derives the bridge.

members.title: No controlled transport across the seventeen decades
members.plain: The top-quark and Higgs numbers come from running Standard Model equations from the Planck scale to the weak scale as if nothing lay between. The lane's own weak-scale formula says sixteen lattice copies switch off along the way, and its own one-step calculation breaks down (the coupling blows up). The running used is a stand-in with unknown error.

members.title: A controlled multiscale flow for gauge fields plus staggered matter exists only in a heavy-mass, zero-coupling corner
members.plain: The repo's most serious attempt to connect the lattice scale to physical scales runs the gauge field and the staggered fermions together through successive coarse-graining steps. It closes only in a corner (extremely heavy fermions, beta = 0). Six named obstacles remain, each independent of the others, so no controlled flow exists for the physical regime.

attack.plain: The wall is real: from a Planck-scale lattice with order-one coupling, ordinary running confines about 18 orders too high, and the repo bridges this only by declaration. Checked to three loops, the repo's own 16 massless tastes give a strong force with no scale at all, and the staircase still blows up near 1e9 GeV. So the gap is not an uncontrolled flow but an unsupplied law for when the 16 tastes switch off, plus one lattice computation.

title: The hierarchy formula: where alpha_LM^16 comes from, what v is, and its trial factors

members.title: Where the sixteen powers of alpha_LM come from (hierarchy magnitude, gate B4 / DELTA0)
members.plain: The weak-scale formula multiplies the Planck scale by sixteen copies of a coupling (about 1/11). The lattice calculation that yields "sixteen" gives sixteen copies of a different number, which shrinks nothing. Swapping one for the other is bookkeeping, not a mechanism. Five ways to make it real were tried and failed; three remain, one of them untried.

members.title: Which quantity is "v" (electroweak-scale readout, endpoint L_t = 4, gate B5)
members.plain: Even if 246.28 GeV comes out, it must be shown to be the size of the Higgs condensate. The formula includes a factor 0.967 that compares a four-step time circle with a two-step one. Nothing selects four steps as physical; an unbounded time circle gives 0.9647 and moves the answer by 0.26%, ten times the claimed 0.026% agreement.

members.title: The headline matches carry undisclosed trial factors
members.plain: Each headline hit (weak scale to 0.03%, top about 172.6, Higgs 125.1) passes through discrete choices made with the answer in view: the exponent, a time-circle length, a colour weight. No note counts how many alternatives were tried. My own small count says a 0.5% hit is not rare. This is a caution on the evidence, not a stuck point.

attack.plain: Nothing in the axioms attaches one factor of the coupling to each of sixteen taste copies, and each route the lane lists (S1, S2, S3, taste-transfer ladder, E1-E5) was already probed and displaced, leaving only non-perturbative or composite forms; this attack does not pass the wall.
