title: Confinement and the mass gap of the physical SU(3) theory are not derived

members.title: Confinement and the mass gap of the physical SU(3) theory are not derived
members.plain: The repo's confinement statement is "this is standard Yang-Mills at beta = 6", taken from the lattice literature. What is actually proved is narrower: a gap for one reduced operator, gap positivity on a small compact box, and toy one-plaquette checks. There is no proof of an area law or infinite-volume gap for the physical 3+1D environment.

attack.plain: The wall's precise core, a proof of the area law and mass gap for pure-glue SU(3) at beta = 6 in infinite volume, is an open problem of mathematical physics that the axioms cannot reach. The repo does not need it: the physical theory has quarks, where the Wilson-loop area law is not the test, and if the repo's 16 massless tastes are right the two-loop flow stops at a fixed point (alpha* = 0.042) and nothing confines. Pure glue on the Planck lattice would confine near 10^18 GeV, so what matters is the taste-threshold law (T30).

title: Weak and hypercharge couplings, alpha_em and the unit charge are not derived

members.title: The SU(2) and U(1) couplings come from a counting ansatz that does not fit SU(3)
members.plain: For the strong force the repo sets g = 1. For the weak and hypercharge forces it uses g^2 = 1/4 and 1/5, taken from counting generators of the Clifford algebra. Nothing derives that counting rule, and it is not applied to SU(3). An older route instead used one unified coupling at the Planck scale. The two routes disagree on the weak coupling's starting value by a factor of 4.6.

members.title: Weak and hypercharge couplings, the mixing angle and the fine-structure constant
members.plain: The weak and hypercharge couplings at the lattice scale (1/4 and 1/5), and so the mixing angle (4/9 at the lattice), are recorded as formal hypotheses, not derivations. The low-energy fine-structure constant needs extra running with thresholds, and the size of atoms needs the electron mass, which is a separate free input. No electromagnetic number is derived.

members.plain: The strength of electromagnetism and the size of the unit charge are free. In the tested models the charged particle either cannot carry a charge that respects full cubic symmetry, or its coupling washes out the field's stiffness. A finite-size comparator estimate of the pure-ring model's own coupling is about 0.3, roughly 40 times the observed 1/137.

attack.plain: Nothing derives the weak or hypercharge coupling: 1/4 and 1/5 are supplied counts, and the unit charge is just a normalization convention. The real question is which single lattice coupling and which single bridge to low energy the three forces share: the observed couplings, extrapolated with Standard-Model content, all come out near 1/4 at the Planck scale (spread 11.5%), but the repo's triple (1, 1/4, 1/5) fits only by running SU(2) and U(1) fully while giving SU(3) no running. Under Standard-Model-content perturbative transport the data ask for g^2 about 0.24 for all three (beta about 25 for SU(3)), which conflicts with T28's g_3^2 = 1 and the alpha_LM^16 hierarchy formula (T31); if they do not share, each factor needs its own supplied tick law and transport.

title: The Higgs doublet, electroweak breaking and the Higgs mass are supplied

members.title: The Higgs doublet is supplied, not derived
members.plain: The axioms give sites, a two-state system per site, a neighbour rule and permanent records. Nothing in them is a field that carries weak charge. The lattice object the lane uses as its Higgs source carries no weak charge at all, and a short proof shows it cannot be turned into a charged pair. So every electroweak note starts from "assume a doublet", and the breaking potential and couplings are copied from the Standard Model.

members.title: Nothing on the lattice action makes the electroweak symmetry break
members.plain: The lattice's own energy curve for the Higgs candidate only slopes downward; it has no valley where the field could settle. Adding the usual attraction term and asking whether a valley appears gives a clear answer at leading order: the lattice sits at 87% of the coupling needed, so nothing condenses. The notes say the breaking must come from structure not yet derived.

members.title: The Higgs mass is the Standard Model run from an admitted boundary
members.plain: Lattice-native calculations give a Higgs mass of 140 or 152 GeV, 12% and 21% too high. The value 125.1 GeV appears only when Standard Model equations, with imported multi-loop coefficients, are run from a Planck-scale condition "quartic coupling = 0" that the notes admit is not derived. It depends strongly on the top coupling: 1% there moves the Higgs mass 3.4 GeV.

attack.plain: Whether a Higgs doublet can exist is decided upstream: it needs fermions that carry no weak charge and a weak force that acts on one handedness only, and the repo's own staggered construction supplies neither (its su(2) either flips left and right or treats them alike). So T34 is the chirality wall (T22) plus the hierarchy wall (T31) plus an already-priced input, and nothing here passes it.

title: The top Yukawa and the absolute mass anchor are uncontrolled

members.title: Top Yukawa, from the exact ratio 1/sqrt(6) to a physical y_t
members.plain: The lane proves an exact number, 1/sqrt(6), for a weak-charge-blind scalar's coupling to quarks. To get the top mass it must show that scalar is the Higgs, carry the value from Planck to weak scale, and correct lattice-to-continuum differences. That last correction was recomputed in June 2026: about +50% and uncontrolled, not -3%. The top mass is "ballpark", 114 to 197 GeV.

members.title: The absolute-mass anchor: the top mass is no longer controlled, and there is no second anchor
members.plain: Ratios among quarks need one absolute mass to become masses. The lane's anchor was the top quark, quoted at 172.57 GeV within 0.07%, from a Planck-scale rule run down to the weak scale. A June 2026 correction found the lattice-to-continuum step was miscounted; that step is uncertain by about 50%, so the top mass is only bracketed at roughly 114-197 GeV. The bottom Yukawa was also set by hand.

members.title: The colour-weight selector (kappa_Y, kappa_EW): sqrt(8/9) and the electroweak couplings
members.plain: A colour-counting choice, whether to keep or drop one of nine colour combinations in a readout, multiplies the top Yukawa by 0.943 and the weak couplings by 1.06. All the framework's good numbers use one choice. The notes prove the axioms do not pick it, and a lattice simulation cannot decide it either.

attack.plain: The top-quark wall is one unknown number, the top's coupling at the Planck scale in weak-scale units. The lattice's exact 1/sqrt(6) reaches it only through a matching nobody can compute at this coupling, a colour selector and a coupling-map choice, so the mass is only bracketed at 114-197 GeV and the 172.6 GeV hit is a roughly 3-bit coincidence. Requiring the Higgs self-coupling and its slope to vanish at the Planck scale fixes the same number with 0.6% spread and gives 174 GeV, but it is an added premise and leaves 4-16% dependence on sibling walls T30, T31, T33.
attack.best_route: R1: Planck-scale double criticality (multiple-point principle, Froggatt-Nielsen 1996) in place of Ward-plus-matching; first artifact y_t(M_Pl)=0.3889, y_t(v)=0.9211, m_t about 174 GeV, a repeat of the April stationarity fan-out.

title: No rule differentiates generations; Yukawa hierarchy free; running cannot make ratios

members.title: No rule makes the three generations of a quark type different (no species-differentiated Yukawa/Ward law)
members.plain: The one clean quark result fixes only the top quark's coupling to the Higgs. Nothing says why up, charm, down, strange and bottom couple with such different strengths. The family symmetry allows at most two distinct values, the gauge rules leave the coupling matrices completely free, and applying the top rule to every quark gets the bottom quark's mass wrong by a factor of about 35.

members.title: The other Yukawa couplings are free
members.plain: Only the top quark has a candidate origin for its coupling. Gauge invariance allows arbitrary 3x3 coupling matrices, and the trick that seems to fix the top makes the bottom quark 35 times too heavy if applied to it. Two absolute mass scales stay free, and the electron sits 5.5 decades below the weak scale with only a loose numerical pattern.

members.title: Scale dynamics cannot produce dimensionless ratios: mass moduli stay free inputs
members.plain: A tempting way to get mass ratios is to let couplings "run" from a high-scale value. The lane tested this in a toy: running only moves the free number to the starting value, so you still put in one number per sector. The lepton mass scale is likewise one free real number, and the Higgs boundary condition is admitted. No mass ratio is fixed by scale dynamics, and the flavour lanes have not fixed them by structure either.

attack.plain: The lattice's rotations treat the three generations exactly like the three directions of space, so no law-level term can tell them apart: in the repo's corner model every rotation-respecting operator on the triplet is a single number. Any split has to come from a non-cubic realized record state, which the registered realized-state primitive classes as registered data; running cannot make ratios either (checked). So the wall is priced at a state-selection input with at least three free shape numbers per Yukawa sector, not solved.

title: Brannen phase delta = 2/9: from an exact fraction to an angle in radians

Each was supplied. The additivity clause was deleted from the Record axiom on 2026-08-13, and K/CPT left the axioms on 2026-06-29. Also, the theorem concerns what records can register; strong CP concerns a phase in the dynamics.

On the repo's even-lattice surface the phase couples to nothing anyway, and where it can couple (nonzero index) the readouts stay blind while the weight carries the phase, with a discrete sign bit that the flavor fits do not fix. So the useful question is whether the lattice supplies an index at all, and how theta-bar is assembled jointly.

The axioms do not say the weight has that form. A two-plaquette term that does carry the twist passes every symmetry test the lane tried. So the zero comes from the chosen class, not from the axioms.

members.plain: To say "the twist angle has a value" you need a whole-number charge counting how the gauge field is wound. Four sub-steps toward a real charge are all open. The lane re-scoped this as not needed for theta-bar = 0. That is true only if W1's premise holds.

title: The CKM atlas's building blocks are supplied identifications

members.title: The CKM atlas's building blocks are supplied identifications, not derivations (and the six-state block is the wrong space)

title: The quark CP phase: why arctan sqrt5

members.title: Where the quark CP phase comes from, and why it is arctan sqrt5
members.plain: Quark CP violation hangs on one phase. The lane gets 65.9 degrees by saying one state out of six is special ("1 plus 5"). Other equally natural splits, 2+4 and 3+3, give 54.7 and 45 degrees. The count of six and the split are put in by hand. The older route instead solves for complex numbers so as to match data.

'One special state of six' cannot be a gauge-invariant operator on the quark block, and discrete-group phases cannot give an irrational multiple of pi, so nothing here derives the angle. The wall reduces to the size ratio (T44) plus a reality structure with one imaginary mass-matrix entry.
attack.best_route: R2/R3: treat the angle as a right angle from one purely imaginary mass-matrix entry (Antusch-King-Malinsky-Spinrath template) plus the real Born-weight ratio |V_td|^2:|V_ub|^2 = 5:1; first artifact is the moduli-plus-texture test already run.
attack.test: Python (t45_test.py, t45_e2_phase_scan.py): commutant of SU(2)xSU(3) on (2,3) is scalars (no gauge-covariant 1+5); delta recovered from four moduli to 1e-9 and real completions miss |V_td| by 1.51x/0.65x; hierarchical textures with one imaginary entry give alpha within 5 deg in 63.5% vs 5.6% for a random phase; 2+4 and 3+3 already excluded at 8.6/16 sigma (CKM fit).
attack.cheaper_question: On 3-dim generation space, derive the real relations |V_td|^2/|V_ub|^2 = 5 and |V_ub|^2 + |V_td|^2 = |V_us V_cb|^2 from a phase-free Born-weight table, and separately why exactly one mass-matrix entry is purely imaginary; the phase and CP nonzero-ness then follow from the moduli.

title: Down-quark route: the 5/6 exponent and the scale choice

members.title: Down-quark route: the 5/6 exponent, the GST relation and the choice of energy scale
members.plain: The lane predicts down-type mass ratios from the mixing numbers with two bridge formulas: |V_us|^2 = m_d/m_s and |V_cb| = (m_s/m_b)^(5/6). So these are the mixing predictions restated, not independent. The exponent 5/6 was the only one of nine group-theory candidates within 10% of the comparator, and only when the two masses are quoted at different energies; at one common energy it is 14% off.

attack.plain: The wall says a power 5/6 turns the mixing number V_cb into the strange/bottom mass ratio, and a scale rule is needed to make it fit. A mass ratio taken at one energy does not change with energy, and there the power law misses by 18.6% (13 sigma); the 0.2% match came from quoting the two masses at different energies, a convention that lets any exponent from 4/5 to 8/9 fit. Running the Standard Model up to the Planck scale barely moves the needed exponent (0.797 to 0.790), so no scale rule is needed and none would help.
attack.best_route: R1: restate the bridge on the RG-invariant m_s/m_b (needs c = 1.153 +- 0.012 or p = 0.7975 +- 0.0024 instead of 5/6); the exponent itself stays the open alignment law (T44, T36, T48).
attack.test: Own four-loop QCD and one-loop SM Yukawa runners: RG-common m_s/m_b = 0.01887 +- 1.2%, bridge +18.6% +- 1.4% (13 sigma) versus +0.20% on the mixed-scale convention; implied exponent 0.7975 +- 0.0024; p(mu) from m_t to M_Pl only 0.797 to 0.790, never 5/6.
attack.cheaper_question: Does |V_cb| = c (m_s/m_b)^p hold with c = 1 on the RG-invariant mass ratio, and what exponent p (data: 0.7975 +- 0.0024, not 5/6) must the up-down alignment law supply?

title: Up-quark route and the Route-2 E-center readout

members.title: Up-quark route: the amplitude law, the up/down partition, and a 10x mismatch in m_c/m_t
members.plain: Each mixing number is the sum of an up-quark and a down-quark part. The lane gives almost all of the 2-3 mixing to the down quarks, which leaves so little for the up sector that the charm-to-top ratio comes out about ten times too small. A free "partition" repairs it, and one amplitude is chosen from a shortlist because it fits. No rule turns that amplitude into a mass.

members.title: The Route-2 E-center readout (target triple -1, -2, 21/4): about 110 notes, no derivation, and the match may be a box-size artifact
members.plain: To fix the up-quark amplitude the lane tried to compute three ratios from how a small 3D lattice box responds to a point source. At one box size (15) they come out near -1, -2 and 5.25. At every other size they are wildly different. About 110 notes have tried to derive the third number; all end in "cannot be derived from what we have".

attack.plain: The wall assumes the up-quark mass ratios come from one 'up amplitude' and from a box-response triple that would fix it. In the repo's own carrier the ratios barely depend on that amplitude (an 18% change moves them 6% and 0.15%); they are set by the mixing numbers, the down ratios and four O(1) coefficients the notes call imported. In boxes 8 times larger the Route-2 triple converges to about (0.98, 1.0, 0.5), not (5/6, -2, 21/4), so the size-15 hit is a finite-box coincidence.
attack.best_route: R3: replace the a_u law and the Route-2 triple by 'what fixes the four NNI coefficients (c12, c23 per sector) from the records', which is T36's generation split and is blocked-equivalent to it.
attack.test: Ran the repo's Route-2 ladder to N=121 with an exact Dirichlet solver (limit q_T 0.984, s_TE about 1.0, rho_E about 0.46 vs 5/6, -2, 21/4; no plateau in probe radius), plus coefficient sensitivity (+-5% moves ratios 9-514%; 0 of 132 blind-prior draws within 10%), a_u elasticity (0.35 and -0.01) and a common-scale check (r_ct +44%).
attack.cheaper_question: What fixes the four geometric-mean NNI coefficients (1.48, 0.65, 0.91, 0.65 in the notes) from the Record and Admissibility axioms? Until they are derived the up-ratio pair is a fit round trip, and a_u and the Route-2 triple are not mass-carrying.

title: Two flavour mechanisms (circulant leptons, tensor/Schur quarks) do not meet

members.title: Two flavour mechanisms that do not meet: the circulant (leptons) and the tensor/Schur atlas (quarks); small CKM vs large PMNS is a supplied contrast
members.plain: The lepton side uses a three-family cyclic structure. If quarks use the same structure, up and down sectors are diagonalised by the same matrix and there is no mixing at all. So the CKM atlas uses a different mechanism, and nothing says why quarks and leptons use different ones, or why quark mixing is small and neutrino mixing large.

attack.plain: A circulant cannot make quarks or leptons mix: two operators that share it commute, and the same holds for the lepton sector (circulant charged leptons plus circulant neutrinos give no PMNS). Mixing is the relative orientation of two operators, and cubic covariance forces every law-level operator on the three-family space to commute, so the orientation is state-level data. A shared seed with sector-dependent masses fits the quark mixing only if the seed is strongly non-circulant, then misses the charged-lepton rotation and neutrino mixing.
attack.best_route: R1: a sector-blind non-circulant seed with sector-dependent diagonal masses (four numbers, fitted to CKM); survives only as a priced fit.
attack.test: Solved for a universal seed reproducing CKM (4 numbers): |R23|/|R12| 0.62-0.87 and |R13|/|R12| 0.05-0.15 (circulant needs 1,1); best circulant misses by 76-93%; it predicts charged-lepton rotation 4-8 deg (12.16 needed) and PMNS 1.4-4.3 box-widths off; the additive form fits V_cb and theta_e but V_ub is x9 and neutrinos come out ~1e8 too heavy; the cubic group's residual-symmetry mixings have smallest off-diagonal 0.577.
attack.price: realized_state_primitive: the sector-relative basis orientation (a sector-blind, non-circulant four-number seed) is S3-breaking state data; law-level cubic covariance makes all triplet operators commute (span{I,J}).

title: Neutrinos: Dirac or Majorana, and the absolute mass scale

members.title: Dirac or Majorana — nothing makes a Majorana mass, nothing forbids one
members.plain: A neutrino could be its own antiparticle if the theory contained one specific extra term. On the current stack that term is exactly zero, so neutrinos come out Dirac by default. Nobody has shown that no admissible extension could switch it on. Until that is decided, the seesaw mechanism, Majorana phases and the neutrinoless-double-beta rate are unavailable, and the answer is left to experiment.

members.title: Absolute mass scale — the two routes to tiny masses cannot both be reached from the stack
members.plain: There are two standard ways to make neutrinos very light: give each a very heavy partner (seesaw), or use an unexplained tiny coupling. The stack switches the first off (W1). Using its own coupling directly gives a neutrino mass about 1 GeV, some twenty billion times too big. The repo's one numerical success uses the seesaw, so it sits on a surface the stack calls empty.

attack.plain: Whether neutrinos are their own antiparticles comes down to whether fermion number is exactly conserved, and the axioms give neither a fermion nor dynamics to decide it. I tested the lane's suggested route in the repo's emergent-fermion model: covariance does not force conservation (with the staggered mass on, a covariant charge-2 term splits the light modes at first order), though the massless light sector is symmetry-protected. So Dirac needs one imposed premise, and the absolute mass scale stays unexplained either way.
attack.best_route: Impose (U1), the dynamics clause commutes with fermion number, and treat any charge-2 coefficient as a further lattice-scale coupling; covariance alone does not supply it (R3 with R2 as the protection statement).
attack.test: Covariance census of pairing forms in the Kawamoto-Smit emergent fermion on 8^3 and 12^3 tori: massless, no covariant pairing for |d|^2<=9 and the 8 light modes have no invariant antisymmetric form (projected Majorana mass <=4e-15); massive, a covariant body-diagonal pairing splits the light levels to m +- 8*lambda.
attack.price: (U1): the dynamics clause conserves fermion number (mu identically 0); not implied by translation and cubic-rotation covariance. The scale (Dirac activation 4.3e-11 or Weinberg coefficient ~1e4 at M_Pl) is a further unpriced premise.

title: The atmospheric-gap success stands on posited bridges

members.title: The one quantitative success stands on posited bridges
members.plain: The lane hits one measured number, the atmospheric mass gap, within a few percent. Getting there needs choices the axioms do not fix: two "minimal lift" rules placing the heavy partners on a ladder, a rule for splitting them, a coupling formula that includes a measured coupling, and a weak-scale value from another lane. The staircase notes behind it have never been audited. A ladder this coarse lands this close by luck roughly once in 70 to 200 tries.

attack.plain: The theory hits the measured atmospheric neutrino mass gap to 3.5%, but only through a chain of choices the axioms do not make. This attack shows that, at the repo's own 5% gate, the hit needs just two bridges (heavy scale = geometric mean of the Planck and weak scales; Dirac coupling = g^2/64) plus two unstated conventions (g read at the Z mass; unreduced Planck mass). The other bridges are idle or smaller than the gate, and the hit is weak evidence: formula-count bounds run from 1.5% to 89%, and the repo's own history shows the formula was chosen against the target.
attack.best_route: R1: restate the claim as the midpoint form m3 = y^2 v^(3/2) M_Pl^(-1/2) with y = g^2/64 (drops the plaquette value, eps/B, k_A and the 7/8 factor; removes the T31 coupling), then pay for the log-midpoint reading and g^2/64 separately.
attack.test: Pre-registered script: chain reproduces +3.52%; the midpoint form (measured v, no alpha_LM) gives -1.8%; g read above 324 GeV, a reduced Planck mass, or an unquenched plaquette (T31 shifts, chain form) each destroy the hit (-12% to -96%); 81 documented variants have coverage 30%, 72 natural coupling forms x 15 rungs have coverage 89% (36% for g^a/2^b only).
attack.price: Log-midpoint reading of the endpoint-exchange lift (M_1 = sqrt(M_Pl v)), y = g(M_Z)^2/64 (ADM-1..3 with g at M_Z), and the unreduced Planck mass 1.2209e19 GeV; equivalence checked to 5% (not an identity), with k_A, eps/B and the (7/8)^(1/4) factor idle or below the gate.

title: The neutrino mass pattern beyond the atmospheric gap is wrong or absent

members.title: The mass pattern beyond the atmospheric gap is wrong or absent
members.plain: Apart from the one good number, the benchmark has the wrong shape: one light state and two nearly equal heavy ones. The "solar" gap comes out about 28 times too large, and the total mass (0.10 eV) exceeds a limit the repo itself quotes. The mixing chart cannot help: its mass-like numbers have a ratio ten times off. No law yet fixes neutrino mass ratios.

attack.plain: The theory's neutrino recipe gives one tiny mass and two nearly equal heavy ones, so the solar mass gap comes out about 28 times too big and the masses sum to 101 meV, above the 72 meV limit the repo quotes. At the retained rungs no choice of the doublet split fixes both the solar and the atmospheric gap (the solar box needs a split near 0.70 and then the atmospheric gap is 9 times too big); both can be met only if the doublet anchor moves by a factor of about 3 and the split is about 0.68, which gives up two of the atmospheric-gap bridges. The one near-pass in the repo (April 2026, split alpha^2, unlanded) compares the wrong pair of masses.
attack.best_route: R3: replace the k_B=8 anchor and the alpha/2 residual sharing by a doublet block with eigenvalue ratio about 5.2 anchored near rung 7.55 (B'/B in [2.90,3.05], r in [0.667,0.687]), which meets both gap boxes with sum 63.6-65.2 meV; nothing derives it.
attack.test: Scanned the lane's own Z3 texture with universal Yukawa (T51_scratch/S1..S5): at retained rungs the joint solar and atmospheric set is empty, 0/72 strict and 0/4212 loose staircase spectra hit both boxes, and the inverted-order reading with r=alpha^2 gets the solar box but loses the atmospheric one and gives sum 101 meV; a random-matrix ensemble puts the observed ratio at 3%.
attack.price: P-a (k_B=8 midpoint anchor) and P-c (residual sharing r=alpha/2) replaced together by a doublet block with eigenvalue ratio about 5.2 near rung 7.55, or else dropping U_e=I for an inverted-order reading (sum 101 meV, atmospheric gap 5.8% low).

title: PMNS mixing angles are set by data; three mixing routes are incompatible

members.title: Mixing angles — the stack gives none, and the extension that gives them is set by the data
members.plain: The theory's own tools give no neutrino mixing. Large mixing appears only after adding an extra piece with three free knobs, and those knobs are set from the measured angles. One proposed rule (three simple equations) sets the knobs so all three angles sit within 1σ of data, but two of its equations are unproved. So the three angles are inputs, not results.

members.title: Three routes to the mixing cannot all be true
members.plain: The repo tells three different stories about the mixing. The chart fits the measured angles. The records story says the middle neutrino is exactly an equal mix of all three flavours, which pushes θ12 outside the current 3σ range unless another unexplained rotation is added. The mass benchmark instead makes the equal-mix state the lightest. On the same operator they give incompatible answers.

attack.plain: The mixing angles are still not derived. But with charged leptons diagonal, one small angle (theta13), a three-way choice among the lane's own symmetry flips (data now favour a flip the lane never tried, giving solar 0.318, atmospheric 0.5, CP phase -90 degrees) and a sign fix all the rest. The three 'incompatible routes' are rival models, and the lane's TM2 package has an error: a Klein-symmetric operator forces theta13 = 0.
attack.best_route: R1: neutrino operator keeps the third Klein flip S.P23 (TM1) plus the mu-tau reflection; first artifact is the TM1 magnitudes lemma and the operator runner (A_v4_branches.py), wounded because the flip is chosen by data and theta13 stays free.
attack.test: Random Hermitian operators per flip (20,000 each): TM2 s12^2 in [0.3404,0.3416] (never in the NuFIT-6.1 3-sigma box), TM1 s12^2 in [0.3168,0.3192] inside it with s23^2=0.5, |sin delta|=1; V4 commutant forces theta13=0; chart baseline branch has s23^2>=0.5351; finite-group catalogue (S3, O_h) never reaches the box (smallest nonzero |U_e3|^2 = 0.0447).
attack.price: One dimensionless C3-doublet-breaking angle (theta13), plus a state selection among three Klein flips and a sign (realized_state_primitive: registered data), plus shared premises U_e = I, electron = fixed corner, sigma_hier, mu-tau reflection, species identification.

title: PMNS CP phase and octant forecast rests on a one-bit sheet choice

members.title: CP phase and octant — the only live prediction rests on a one-bit sheet choice and leans against current data
members.plain: The lane's sharp forecast is a CP-violation phase near −90° with the atmospheric angle above 45°. The phase's sign is a one-bit choice the theory cannot make: flipping one constant mirrors it exactly. The quoted range was built when data favoured it. The repo's own NuFIT-6.1 comparison puts the current best fit outside the range and the angle below 45°. DUNE and Hyper-K will decide.

attack.plain: The CP-phase and octant forecast rests on two hidden yes/no labels, not one: the sign of the imaginary link and which row is called muon versus tau. The second label alone sets the 'upper octant', and the repo's octant selector is circular because its threshold already assumes that labelling. What the chart predicts under every labelling is a near-maximal CP phase (within 11 degrees of plus or minus 90) and a band around maximal theta23 that is excluded; the labels themselves are not derived and would be set by two measured signs.
attack.best_route: R1: forecast the label-free content (|sin dCP| >= 0.98, s23^2 outside (0.459, 0.541)) and treat the two labels as one relative-orientation bit plus an octant side, priced at the parked reflection decision or a shared-axis bridge to the charged-lepton frame.
attack.test: Four-sheet enumeration of the repo chart (gamma sign x sigma pairing), a mirror-threshold check, and a float re-run of the band over the NuFIT-6.1 box: identities held in 400 random chart points; threshold 0.540970 for (2,1,0) mirrors to 0.459030 for (2,0,1); band over the 6.1 box is 258.98-269.61 deg (partner sheet 270.39-281.02 deg), inside the certified 251.86-270.00.
attack.cheaper_question: Are the label-free statements true (delta_CP within 11 degrees of plus or minus 90; s23^2 outside (0.459, 0.541)), and is the single relative-orientation bit (sign of the source cubic times parity of the mu-tau pairing) plus the octant side settled by data instead of derived?

title: The dark-matter candidate has incompatible charges and identities

members.title: The notes give the dark state incompatible charges, and offer three mutually exclusive dark candidates
members.plain: Different dark-matter notes describe different particles. One says the dark particle feels no force but gravity, is Planck-mass, and cannot be tested. Another treats it as a 3.9 TeV particle that annihilates through a gauge-like force, and its mass derivation needs it to carry colour charge. A third calls a right-handed neutrino the "DM candidate", though that particle decays in about 10^-30 seconds. These cannot all hold.

attack.plain: The dark-matter notes disagree on charges because they use two embeddings and two meanings of 'singlet', but a landed note already settles the embedding: the eight taste states are one generation of left-handed doublets, with no gauge singlet, so 'dark = gauge-singlet taste state' is dead and the mass step's 'dark' state has quark-doublet charges. The only gauge singlet in the landed matter content is a right-handed neutrino, and the notes' candidate N1 of that kind lives about 2e-30 s. No dark candidate results; the real question is whether any stable neutral state exists, which belongs to the neutrino-mass, dark-mass and coupling walls.
attack.best_route: Route A (reframe on landed content: ask which landed state is gauge-neutral and stable; only nu_R, and N1 fails); the fallback is the nuMSM-style role split (decoupled lightest right-handed neutrino, Asaka-Shaposhnikov PLB 620 (2005) 17), which needs T49 and a Yukawa near 1e-13 and abandons 16 v.
attack.test: T54_scratch/t54_test.py: for each of the 3 choices of weak-fibre axis, C^8 = 6 x (3,2)_{1/3} + 2 x (1,2)_{-1} with zero gauge singlets and S0/S3 = (C_F 4/3, j(j+1) 3/4, Y +1/3); the three axis-conjugates generate all su(8) (irreducible); one-generation Fock space has neutral states only at k=0,8; N1 tau = 1.8e-30 s with the seesaw Yukawa (needs y 2e-24 smaller for stability); landed runner re-run 61 PASS.
attack.cheaper_question: Does the landed matter content contain any gauge-neutral state that can be stable and gravitating? (Answer: only the right-handed neutrino, and N1 is not; that is T49, T55, T56.)

title: The dark mass 16 v was found by scanning against the target

members.title: The dark mass 16 v was found by scanning against the abundance target, and no mechanism exists
members.plain: The dark mass, 16 times the electroweak scale (3.94 TeV), was found by searching a list of framework numbers for one that makes the observed baryon asymmetry come out. Every attempt to explain why the mass should be 16 v has failed, been corrected, or stayed a numerical coincidence. So the mass is a fit to the answer, not a prediction.

attack.plain: The dark-matter abundance only measures mass divided by the annihilation coupling (42.6 TeV, i.e. the thermal cross-section 2.0e-26 cm^3/s), so 16 v cannot be a mass prediction on its own; it is one of several (mass, coupling) pairs that land on that ratio. A random target is hit by the note's own list 17-25% of the time, and 42-97% once the couplings already on file are also free. The lane's proposed mechanism does not give 16 v either: the Higgs-parallel effective-potential reading gives 9.1 v.
attack.best_route: R3: drop m_DM as a stand-alone target and ask for the annihilation strength pi*alpha_X^2/m^2 (or m/alpha_X) once the dark charges are fixed (R2, Minimal Dark Matter ordering, blocked-equivalent to T54); first artifact is Tests A and C.
attack.test: T55_scratch/t55_test.py: Lambda*=m/alpha_X=42,572 GeV=172.9 v (<sigma v>=2.02e-26 cm^3/s), base rate of a family hit at a random target 0.17-0.25, pair hits within 5% at the real target: (16 v, alpha_LM) +2.1%, (R_base v, 1/16pi) +0.2%, (8 v, 0.048) -3.6% (random-target pair coverage 0.42-0.97 by coupling list), and the T1 effective-potential ladder gives 0.57, 2.28, 9.12, 36.5 v with none near 15.67 v.
attack.cheaper_question: What annihilation strength pi*alpha_X^2/m^2 (equivalently m/alpha_X) does the framework fix once the dark state's charges are fixed, and is it the thermal value 2e-26 cm^3/s? The abundance alone cannot select a mass.

title: The dark annihilation coupling is chosen, not derived

members.title: The annihilation force and the coupling in the Sommerfeld factor are chosen, not derived
members.plain: How much dark matter survives depends on how strongly it annihilates. The notes pick the coupling from a range: 0.03 to 0.05 in one note, about 0.091 to 0.092 in others, and these give different answers. A dark particle that feels no gauge force would not have that coupling at all. The resulting dark-to-ordinary ratio comes out 1.5 to 2% above the measured 5.36.

attack.plain: The annihilation coupling is not a separate free number: it is the running gauge coupling of whatever force the dark state feels, so it is fixed once the dark state's charges and conjugacy (T54) and the lattice couplings at TeV scale (T28-T30, T33) are supplied. For the coloured reading that gives alpha_X = 0.0785 and 16 v overshoots the dark density by about a factor 2. The lane's two coupling pins (0.048 and 0.0907) are one pin seen through a factor-2 error in its Sommerfeld code, and no single coupling closes its eta chain.
attack.best_route: Minimal-DM template: set alpha_X to the gauge coupling of the dark representation at mu = m (coloured Dirac triplet, colour-resolved Sommerfeld); first artifact is the fixed-channel table, and the open obligation is a bound-state boost of about +96% to reach 16 v.
attack.test: Rebuilt the lane's Sommerfeld kernel exactly (R = 5.442020, 5.482856), checked the Coulomb factor against the radial Schroedinger equation (2 pi form right, lane's pi form off by 2 in argument), solved freeze-out numerically at 16 v: coloured Dirac triplet with alpha_s(m) = 0.0785 gives Omega h^2 = 0.235 (x1.96), self-conjugate counting 0.117, dark U(1) at alpha_LM 0.079-0.254; channel ambiguity spans x6.6; single-alpha eta closure misses by -28% or +356%.
attack.price: The dark state's gauge representation and conjugacy (T54/T26) plus the TeV-scale gauge couplings from the lattice (T28-T30, T33); the rest (x_F, g*, bound states) is standard cosmology (T59).

title: R = R_base x S is a group-theory identity presented as the dark-to-baryon ratio

members.title: R = R_base x S is a group-theory identity presented as the physical dark-to-baryon density ratio
members.plain: The number 31/9 is exact arithmetic on group-theory constants. Nothing shows why the real ratio of dark to ordinary matter should equal it. The lane's own earlier note showed that ordinary matter is left over from a matter-antimatter imbalance, not from annihilation freeze-out, so a ratio of annihilation strengths cannot give it. Later notes reuse the number to compute the imbalance.

attack.plain: 31/9 is correct group-theory arithmetic, but nothing in the framework makes it the real dark-to-ordinary matter density ratio: on the lane's own formulas, treating ordinary matter as an annihilation leftover is off by a factor of about 750,000, and every way of linking the two densities needs one new non-group-theory number. The ratio is only ever used to derive the baryon asymmetry, which then carries no information beyond one comparison of the dark-matter density with data, so the ratio should stop being a derived quantity.
attack.best_route: Route B: drop R as a derived quantity and ask for Omega_DM h^2 alone with eta imported as data (0.1275, band 0.112-0.143 vs 0.1200); keeping R physical costs one new number (eps ~ 1e-8 or T_d ~ m/10), blocked-equivalent to T58.
attack.test: T57_scratch/t57_test.py: symmetric-relic baryons give R_sym = 4.1e6 (lane formula) / 6e9 (hadronic sigma) vs 5.48; linked-origin needs n_DM/n_b = 1.3e-3 at 16 v (no small rational) or m_DM = 1.7-51 GeV at rational ratios; charge sensitivity R_base = 31/9, 3/5, 93/128 or undefined; look-elsewhere 3.6%/5.1% of alternative bases also match (my pre-registered guess of 10-25% missed).
attack.cheaper_question: Does the dark sector alone give Omega_DM h^2 = 0.120 (with eta imported as data), so that R is an output compared with data rather than a derived group-theory number?

title: The baryon asymmetry is imported; leptogenesis and its CP sign are not derived

members.title: The baryon asymmetry eta is imported, and both derivation routes are blocked
members.plain: The lane needs the amount of ordinary matter, which comes from the matter-antimatter imbalance eta, and takes it from observation. The neutrino route to eta gives 0.19 of the observed value. Reaching 1.0 needs a neutrino-phase sign that no note can derive, and about thirty notes close the alternative routes. The old electroweak route stalls on undetermined inputs.

members.title: The baryon asymmetry is reached only by choosing a point, and its CP sign has no source
members.plain: The lane's clean calculation gives a baryon asymmetry about five times too small (0.19 of observed). A more elaborate version reaches exactly the observed value, but only by choosing a point in a family of solutions. What is left is one sign: which way CP violation points. Every selector in the lane is blind to that sign, and a separate no-go says the tested routes cannot source it.

members.title: The leptogenesis machinery is not in the four axioms
members.plain: To make a matter excess you need heavy neutrinos, a hot expanding bath, standard-model particle counts and a process that turns lepton number into baryon number. The lane supplies each as a named packet. Its audit-critical upstream steps were flagged as needing new derivations from the axioms, and none exists. Without them the chain is arithmetic on supplied inputs.

attack.plain: The baryon-asymmetry wall has no obstruction of its own. The lane's chain needs heavy Majorana neutrinos (which the neutrino lane says the current stack sets to zero), a hot expanding bath, a CP source and one sign choice. Its size is set by the heavy-neutrino scale and the CP amplitude, not by the imported weak coupling, and its sign is the same one bit as the PMNS CP-phase forecast (T53).
attack.best_route: Route B (misframing): first ask whether covariant Admissibility permits DeltaN=2 (L10-W1 test); if not, Dirac leptogenesis (Dick-Lindner-Ratz-Wright 2000). Route A (sign fixed by existence of matter, giving a sin(dCP) prediction) is the best sign reduction.
attack.test: Reproduced the lane's chain: eta/eta_obs = 0.188785929502 (3e-13). Slope vs g_weak is -0.65 (maximum over g_weak 0.50), vs M1 +1.16; reaching 1 needs CP amplitude x5.3 or M1 x4.0. abs() in the code discards the physical sign; sin(dCP)<0 follows gamma>0 in only 83% of the chamber (8/8 in the data box).
attack.price: Conjunction of T49/T50 (Majorana M_R != 0 and the M1 ladder), T59 with T25 (thermal bath, H_rad, particle inventory) and T53 (the PMNS sheet bit, the T23 orientation datum); once supplied only checked arithmetic remains.

title: Cosmic history (expansion, thermal state, abundances) is supplied

members.title: The thermal, cosmic-history substrate of a relic abundance is imported
members.plain: A relic abundance is a statement about a hot, expanding early universe cooling past a freeze-out point. The axioms give no time metric, no expansion law, no thermal state and no starting condition. The framework's cosmology inputs (Friedmann law, particle count, today's temperature, freeze-out constant) are imported or conditional, and the repo's current rule is that an unresolved cosmology input supplies no premise.

members.title: Expansion has no native meaning under the axioms; the Friedmann backdrop is supplied
members.plain: The lattice is fixed and the axioms have no time metric or gravity. The cosmology stack assumes a uniform, smoothly expanding universe obeying the Friedmann equations with a standard matter and radiation mix. The lane's own open gate lists three of those assumptions as supplied. The newest lattice work gets Friedmann-like equations only after a length-growth law is supplied.

members.title: Matter and dark-energy fractions today need cosmic-history numbers the axioms do not supply, and "why now" has no route
members.plain: Once the cosmic size is fixed, the fractions of matter and dark energy today need one more number about cosmic history. The lane proved the axioms do not supply it and found two ways it could come. One runs through the baryon asymmetry and a coupling; the other, a direct derivation, has no candidate. Nothing explains why matter and dark energy are comparable now.

attack.plain: The wall bundles a real gravity-side obligation with items that are not walls. In a supplied Boltzmann model the relic yield forgets any thermal start before about 0.9 of the freeze-out point, reads the expansion rate only over about two decades of time near freeze-out, and needs history only through T_0, so the thermal state, x_F and the Kolb-Turner constant are outputs or an inequality. The expansion law is the gravity wall's price (a posited scale variable), which block 146 already turns into radiation and matter branches inside its own model; the cosmic numbers (H_0 a, Omega_Lambda) are irreducible data.
attack.best_route: R1: split law, state and data; the one law obligation left is the radiation-era H(T) with exponent 2 (make block 146's homogeneous model non-ansatz), the rest is T_0, H_0 a and Omega_Lambda as data.
attack.test: T59_test.py (scipy Boltzmann ODE, sympy, flat LCDM integrals): yield spread 2e-11 over starts x_i<=8 and <=3e-11 to x_i=22 (x_F=27.2), 0.5 at x_i=27; kernel 5-95% window x=22.6-220 (2 decades of time); Y(q=1)/Y(q=2)=37; block 146 branches satisfy Friedmann iff alpha=K/4 (exact); particle horizon/(c t0)=3.25-3.44 so a fixed lattice at <=1 site/tick is short by >=34x in volume; age at fixed t0 leaves H_0 spread 58.9-82.0 over Omega_Lambda 0.5-0.85.
attack.cheaper_question: Given block 146's homogeneous model (the T64 posit of a scale variable plus alpha = K/4), can the radiation-era exponent q=2 and its coefficient be made non-ansatz (zero-mode compatibility), with T_0, H_0 a and Omega_Lambda left as three data?

title: Vacuum energy and the zero of energy

members.title: Vacuum energy is about 10^123 too big and no mechanism removes it
members.plain: Adding up the energy of empty space on the lattice gives about one Planck unit per cell. Observed dark energy is about 10^-123 of that. The lane tried five ways to shrink the sum and none worked. The newest lattice work shows the lattice's empty-space energy is not even constant as the lattice stretches, so it does not act like a cosmological constant.

members.title: What gravitates: the member's zero mode tests the zero of energy (vacuum energy)
members.plain: It is not settled whether gravity sees the vacuum. The walker's filled sea carries about one hop of negative energy per site. If the gravity field sees it, a closed lattice bounces or cannot move at all; if not, the framework has to supply the zero of energy by hand. This is the cosmological-constant problem in the lattice's own terms.

attack.plain: Gravity's vacuum energy is not one number here: the walker's filled sea holds about 1.19 Planck units per site, and every way of choosing the zero of energy just moves that quantity around (as the sea, as its removal, or as record birth cost) or leaves a mass-squared remainder 64 to 89 decades too big. No single zero works for a universe that runs from few records to many, so the zero has to depend on the record count, which the axioms do not supply. The 1e-123 itself is the cosmos size of T62 in other units.
attack.best_route: R3: state the source's zero as the same-record-number ground energy (energy above the sea at fixed record count), with the source reading chosen by hand, and hand the number 1e-123 to T62; first artifact is the exact per-density leftover table.
attack.test: t60_free.py and t60_hardcore.py: reproduced the wall's numbers (I = 1.193801, 2I = 2.387602 = probe 4's birth cost); p/rho = 1/3 exactly for free and hard-core sea; stretch dilution needs a = 9.3e-5 m (15 decades over collider reach), a = 1e-19 m leaves 8e-64 (60 decades too big); records-only remainder 64-89 decades too big and massless weight 0; exact hard-core 4x4 shows every fixed zero leaves 100% of e_min at some density; no equilibrium (dE/d ell > 0).
attack.price: Z: the source's zero of energy is the energy of the same-record-number ground state (energy above the sea at fixed record count), with the source reading (records-only or amplitude) chosen by hand; the realized state's record density is registered data, and 1e-123 is T62's R_Lambda/a.

title: A fixed regular lattice brings Planck-size shape and mass-type terms that must be tuned

members.title: Order-one lattice-scale numbers against a tiny observed vacuum: the tuning demands
members.plain: With a Planck-size lattice and order-one numbers, the vacuum carries order-one lattice-scale energy and shape stiffness. The gravity probe found that a field laid over the grid gets mass-like terms of Planck size unless at least two more numbers are tuned, on top of the cosmological constant. That is fitting under another name.

members.title: A fixed regular lattice gives the graviton mass-type terms and destabilising shear energy unless several numbers are tuned
members.plain: A regular grid has a shape. Couple the walker's vacuum to a constant metric in the natural way and its energy changes when the metric shears the grid, which costs nothing in real gravity. That acts like a graviton mass of the vacuum's size unless several numbers are tuned, and for interacting matter the cancellation returns at the next order. I reproduced the basic numbers.

attack.plain: A fixed grid has a shape and a gravity wave changes shape, so the grid's vacuum resists the wave with a Planck-sized, wrong-sign (growth) term; free particles can be fixed by a designed coupling, interacting ones cannot. New here: for any cubic-symmetric fermion matter whose hopping is linear in the metric, interacting or not, the shear coefficient is negative and at least one twelfth of the hopping energy per cell, so no interaction cancels it. Passing needs an exact shear Ward identity (a local conserved momentum that is not a hopping walker's Fourier momentum), which is T17's premise; otherwise three or more numbers are tuned to about 1e-71 at best.
attack.best_route: R2/R3: decide T17's fork first (label momentum vs Fourier momentum); first artifact is an odd-charge census of the classical moving-records clause V* plus the check that it carries a wave-supporting vacuum; random discreteness (Poisson sprinkling, exact shear-blind mean) is the only other exit and drops the Lattice axiom.
attack.test: Own reproduction of P6 (E0=-1.193801, c_E=-0.17793, c_T=-0.14667; designed vs natural coupling share node metrics to 1e-10 but shift energy -3e-9 vs -7.1e-3), exact diagonalisation of an interacting 2D walker (12,870 states, V=0..2): E concave in the hop metric, c_vp<0 at every V and below K/8, needed seagull varies with V; O_h/hypercubic counting 3 vs 2 mass forms for a rank-2 field; arithmetic squeeze (untuned pass needs a>=9e-10 m vs matter tests a<~2e-27 m).
attack.price: Pi: wave-carrying interacting lattice matter has an exact local shear (momentum-stress) Ward identity, i.e. a local conserved odd charge other than a hopping walker's Fourier momentum (T17's premises F and E); T61 is the price of dropping E: at least three O_h mass numbers tuned at every order, about 1e-71 at the finest spacing matter tests allow (reading) and 1e-103 at Planck.

title: The size of the cosmos (R_Lambda/a, H_0) is put in by hand; S^3 versus flat

members.title: The size of the cosmos (R_Λ/a ≈ 10^61) and H_0 are put in by hand
members.plain: The lane proves a tidy formula, Λ = 3/R², but the radius R, in lattice units, is not derived. The quoted agreement (a factor 1.44 off) uses the measured Hubble rate. The notes say what is missing is a way to fix R without the observed H_0, and a gravity input (lattice spacing equal to the Planck length) that no one has derived.

members.title: The 3-sphere behind Λ = λ₁(S³) may be a renaming, and it clashes with the flat space used elsewhere
members.plain: To get Λ the lane treats space as a 3-sphere of radius R. To get the expansion, matter fractions and baryon asymmetry it assumes space is flat. A sphere of the size that gives the observed Λ would make space visibly curved, which observation rules out. The "identity" also only says a de Sitter universe of radius R has Λ = 3/R², which is geometry, not a derivation.

attack.plain: The wall is really three things. The sphere-versus-flat clash is a label clash: the sphere identity holds only at the instant a closed de Sitter universe is at rest, so it never meets the flat premise. The Hubble rate is a date (age in ticks), which the repo files as data. What remains is one number, Lambda in Planck units (~3e-122), which is the vacuum-energy wall in other units; counting records cannot give it unless records are ordered.
attack.best_route: R2: treat Lambda as realized-state data under a trace-free (unimodular/sequestering) gravity class; first artifact is a trace-free field equation on the lattice member (needs T67/T64).
attack.test: Exact sympy geometry, unit map, counting-exponent table and 3D lattice number-variance runs: S^3 gap equals Lambda only at H=0; R_Lambda/a is rho_vac/rho_P in other units; creations-only counting is off by 31 decades; random local formation gives variance ~ w^3 (Fano factor saturates), so only ordered records reach exponent 2.
attack.price: R_Lambda/a is T60's vacuum-energy number rho_vac/rho_P (with T70's G/a^2) in other units, plus epoch data (realized_state_primitive); the only registry-legal status is a registered realized-state datum under a supplied trace-free gravity class (T67/T64).

title: Inflation and the primordial spectrum are asserted

members.title: Inflation and the primordial spectrum are asserted, not derived
members.plain: The lane "predicts" the spectral tilt by growing a graph and counting random noise. The correction that makes it match slow-roll inflation is written in without derivation, the number of e-folds (60) is put in, and a claim that 10^78 nodes "matches" the 10^183 Planck cells in the universe is off by about 105 orders of magnitude. A growing graph is not in the axioms either.

attack.plain: The lane's tilt comes from a growth profile, 60 e-folds and a correction term that are all put in, and its only measurement sees seed nodes plus white noise, not growth. Growth of the needed size is impossible on the fixed grid with one light cone (at most about 19 e-folds fit), and local record rules give white large-scale fluctuations, so a scale-free spectrum with amplitude 2.1e-9 has to be a property of the starting state.
attack.best_route: R3: split growth, shape and amplitude, and register (n_s, A_s, coherence beyond the light cone) as realized-state data with T16's past hypothesis; the wounded live route is R2, the infinite-volume small-k exponent of a critical conserved crowding-hop pattern.
attack.test: Runner audit (edges unused; Poisson control n_s = 4.07 = 1 + d; runner n_s runs +2.24 to -0.51 over f = 2..8 while the formula runs -1.89 to +0.04); structure factors of local record patterns (alpha_eff about 0 for crowding and Eden, +0.25 at L = 32 and +0.37 at L = 48 for a critical hop rule); cone bound gives N_e max 17-19 against 60; static-pattern amplitude 1e-186 to 7e-248 against 2.1e-9.
attack.price: The primordial record configuration's long-wavelength correlation structure (tilt n_s, amplitude A_s, coherence beyond the light cone) is registered realized-state data under realized_state_primitive, together with the past hypothesis (T16); wounded: the infinite-volume exponent of a critical hop class and a time-dependent amplitude are not excluded.

title: No finite-site graviton with Einstein's spectrum (the gravity wall; exercised 2026-09-29)

members.title: No finite-site graviton with Einstein's spectrum (too slow, or a wobble comes with it)
members.plain: Einstein's gravity waves have two fingerprints: light speed, and one shape only, a stretch-and-squeeze across the direction of travel. Every way tried to build them from finite, record-like pieces on the fixed grid misses one. Strict local rules make the waves crawl. Loosening the rules makes them light-fast but adds a sideways wobble the double pulsar excludes unless it runs more than twelve times faster. Only continuous numbers at each site have worked.

members.title: Einstein's wrong-sign conformal mode is needed, and a ground state cannot supply it
members.plain: Einstein's own theory has one direction, the overall size of space, whose energy runs backwards; his time rule hides it. To remove the wobble from a lattice graviton, the lattice would need that backwards-running direction too. A system in its lowest-energy state cannot have it. Forcing it gives a knife edge, a ghost and a flat gapless band. The same sign problem shows up in every gravity lane.

members.title: A composite graviton's extra modes have no known gapping mechanism
members.plain: One way out keeps finite sites and exact rules: build the graviton as a bound state of simpler fields, for example three photon-like fields. It can look light-speed and pure at first, but its unwanted partners then have to be removed by some strong-coupling effect. None is known. The one literature candidate, from Gu and Wen, is called unreliable by its own authors.

members.title: Gravity as an equation of state of entanglement does not work on the fixed cubic grid
members.plain: One way to avoid a graviton field is to get Einstein's equation from how entanglement grows with area. On this grid the entanglement per unit area differs by 16–18 % between cut orientations, so there is no single coefficient, and the derivation needs a metric and boosts the axioms do not supply. I reproduced the orientation difference with my own code.

title: The owner-level gravity exits that keep finite sites have no bounded test

members.title: The two owner-level exits that keep the axioms' finite sites (recorded adjacency; strongly correlated or non-local gravity) have no bounded test
members.plain: If continuous numbers per site are refused, two choices remain: let the grid's connections themselves be the geometry, or say gravity is a strongly interacting many-body pattern with no simple wave description. For neither is there a test anyone can run. The first also makes the Record axiom circular, because records sit on sites that would then be made of records.

attack.plain: The two exits (a recorded, changeable grid; gravity as a strongly interacting or non-local pattern) are not two separate doors with no tests. Bounded necessary-condition tests exist and I ran three: a periodic recorded grid keeps its cubic anisotropy and carries the metric only as a density of records (exit C), graded lengths are the finite-slot wall (T64), and only an aperiodic state is new, replacing the Lattice axiom wholesale; the non-local exit needs a partner-gapping kernel whose range grows with the wavelength. No graviton was found or excluded.
attack.best_route: R4 misframing: replace 'find a model' by a necessary-condition battery (ground-state isotropy, polarisation content, kernel range), then settle T77 (are exact balance laws outputs of directed formation).
attack.test: Ran isotropy (step-count norm anisotropy 1.41 in the 26-star, Poisson graphs isotropic to 1%), diluted-Z3 metric density (rank 6, linear to 5%; a fixed polarisation is 40/40/20 percent TT/helicity 1/helicity 0) and a non-local kernel truncation (rho ~ 1 for R<=4; needs R ~ 4/|q|, tail r^-3.07).
attack.cheaper_question: Which ground state does recorded adjacency choose (periodic grid, graded lengths, or aperiodic), since each lands in an already-named wall; and can exit C's tensor balance law be an output of directed local formation (T77)?

title: Nonlinear closure of gravity's constraint algebra on the fixed lattice

members.title: Nonlinear closure of gravity's constraint algebra on the fixed lattice
members.plain: Einstein's theory hangs together only if its rules keep working when the field is strong, not just for small waves. On a fixed grid that is known to be hard, because the tools that guarantee it fail for lattice brackets. At small amplitude the clock rules close only at one special ratio. Beyond that the walker's clocks close only for uniform lapses. The test that would settle the next order is not yet specified.

attack.plain: The map's test A1, whether gravity's time-and-space rules stay consistent at second order in the field on a fixed grid, was never specified or run. I specified it and ran it in one- and two-direction reduced sectors with any local rule of range up to 2, and it passes with Einstein's continuum limit, so the expected failure is not there at second order. The wall stays open in full 3D, beyond second order, and in the matter cross-terms (block 150), where only nearest-neighbour relabellings are excluded.
attack.best_route: Run the same exact-linear-algebra pipeline on a 3x3x3 window with cube symmetry and all six components, then close the walker's lapse bracket against range-2 relabellings (block 150 H5 with range-2 xi).
attack.test: Second-order lapse-lapse identity as exact/float linear systems: planar 1D consistent at range 1-3 (exact mod two primes) and 2D shear sector, 3x3 window, 15,215 D4-orbit unknowns, ADM-matched consistent (residual 1.2e-9 of 118); wrong targets leave 6e-3 to 1.2e-2 against 3e-7.

title: The geometric carrier is supplied; no Record-to-geometry map; Einstein's action not derived

members.title: The geometric carrier (metric, clock rate, lengths, tensor slots) is supplied; there is no Record-to-geometry map
members.plain: Every working piece of gravity in the repository starts from something the axioms do not contain: a metric with continuous lengths and angles, a tick rate per site, or a tensor field. The step from records to geometry has never been built: no records-to-event-order map, no derived clock rate, no lengths from records. Gravity therefore comes out only relative to a supplied geometry.

members.title: Einstein's action itself is not derived (direct route blocked; induction needs the metric posit and may not give the Einstein form)
members.plain: Even given a metric, the repository has not shown that the lattice produces Einstein's gravitational action. The direct route from the determinant of the Dirac operator lacks a step. The induced-gravity route needs the metric to exist as a field, and on a fixed lattice it may not give the Einstein form at all, only mass-like terms and direction-dependent speeds.

members.title: No positive physical reconstruction of a lattice gravity action has been found; the reflection-positivity route has only negative finite results and its bridge is parked
members.plain: The older "gravity mainline" tried to make a lattice gravity action pass a positivity test, so that it defines a real quantum theory with only positive-norm states. In every finite case tried it failed: the reflected-curvature action has wrong-sign spin-2 modes and an extra indefinite channel. The route was called closed, but the landed notes were corrected to claim only their finite fixtures. What remains is a parked owner decision.

attack.plain: The axioms give only a graph of sites, and every working gravity carrier needs numbers the graph lacks. Bond lengths on nearest-neighbour edges are either pure relabelling or carry a cutoff-size mass, and the order in which records form has no macroscopic light cone. What is left to supply is six shear numbers per vertex on second-neighbour pairs, plus a relabelling symmetry of the action (linear order only).
attack.best_route: Plaquette (4-cycle) record functionals as the six shear numbers, with the cone taken from the dynamics generator; first artifact is an equivariant-map count plus the gauge-closure check with plaquette-defined diagonals (wounded: relabelling inertness has no source on a fixed lattice).
attack.test: Ran the repository's own 15x15 Regge Hessian restricted to nearest-neighbour axis edges (frozen: Q_aa(0) eigenvalues -18,-2,-2,-2, gauge leakage 0.50; relaxed: Q_eff = 0 to 1e-12; control with 6 face diagonals: rank 6, gauge closure 7e-14), a cubic-group character count (shear T2 first appears at second neighbours), and a causal-order simulation (iid/blind clock futures average 17 sites, extent <= 10, L-independent).
attack.price: Independent shear/plaquette variables at second-neighbour scale (six numbers per vertex) with a relabelling-inert (embedding-inert) action, both supplied; T64's option A sharpened.

title: The curvature member (light bending x2) is declared, not forced

members.title: The curvature member (and so light bending by twice the Newtonian value) is declared, not forced
members.plain: The clock-only law bends light by half the Einstein value. Getting the full factor needs the lattice also to stretch space near a body, which the clock law does not do: a body at rest sources no lengths. The repository gets the factor 2 by declaring an action whose exponent, linearity in the clock rates, stiffness and sign are chosen rather than derived.

attack.plain: Clock-only gravity bends light by half the Einstein amount, and the repository gets the full amount by declaring an energy for stretching space. If the gravitational field is a tensor that looks the same after relabelling points in space and time, most of the declared numbers are forced at weak field (lapse-linearity, the curvature form, Einstein's kinetic normalisation and the conformal sign), and the bending factor becomes exactly (matter speed / gravity speed)^2. So 'bends x2' is the same premise as 'gravity waves move at light speed' (T14), not a separate declaration.
attack.best_route: Impose full linearised relabelling invariance (incl. time-space mixing) on the tensor member; the rate-linear curvature ledger then equals the one-light-cone point K_m = K_s (alpha = K/4), which the hypercubic tick or matter-closure (b150) must supply.
attack.test: Exact sympy classification of quadratic symbols: spatial-cubic+time-reversal forms 26 -> 2 under relabelling invariance (B4: 9 -> 1); in all 7 probed members and 4 k-directions the solved static gamma equals K_m/K_s = 1/(TT speed)^2, K_m = 2 alpha, c_k = -24 alpha, no lapse-squared term; the K_m = K_s member is the hypercubic Fierz-Pauli member (gamma = 1).
attack.price: The member's cone equals the matter cone (K_m/K_s = 1, equivalently alpha = K/4), plus linearised relabelling invariance of the tensor member; this is T14's one-speed premise (L14-W16).

title: The source/action bridge: what sources gravity and with what readout

members.title: The source/action bridge: what sources gravity, and with what absolute strength and unit
members.plain: Gravity has to know what makes it: energy, a record count, or a compressed density, and with what strength. The axioms list "source/action identification" as an open gate. The lattice lane assumes the source is the walkers' energy when a ledger is kept. Nobody has derived that assumption, and the strength is still free.

members.title: The source-to-action and log-det readout bridge lost its footing when Record additivity was removed
members.plain: The older route from the lattice to an action ran through "the total of a group of records is the sum of the parts". That sentence was removed from the axioms on 2026-08-13, so the log-determinant generating function and what was built on it lost its support. The link from an action to physical sources and readings (charge, mass, gravity) was named open in eight places and remains so.

attack.plain: The source half is not a separate wall: once gravity's carrier is the local tick rate multiplying the whole local Hamiltonian, the source is that Hamiltonian's energy density (landed, b55), and the tensor version is the momentum-books wall (T64). The strength half, tried through the readout (the filled sea's energy, the zero-temperature log-det), gives a definite positive stiffness for the clock field, but its size depends on the supplied walk and it sits under a volume term twelve times larger with the wrong sign, so the sea alone repels rather than attracts.
attack.best_route: R2: read the filled sea's energy as the action (Sakharov-style); first artifact is the exact Brillouin-zone stiffness kappa = 0.0994 for the landed 3D walk, which still needs the sea's zero of energy cancelled (T60).
attack.test: Exact k-space second-order sea energy for H = sum sigma_a sin k_a under phi H phi, checked against exact diagonalisation (<=8e-11) and the 1D free-sea kappa = 1/(3 pi) (3e-6): 3D c0 = -1.1938, kappa = 0.0994 (declared 0.095 is about 4.5% below), isotropic to 0.2%, walk-dependent (0.086-0.153 over two walk families, 28.9% spread on the registered set), Hessian negative at every q and zero at the chessboard corner, |c0| = 12.0 kappa; with c0 cancelled G_lat = 1/(4 pi kappa) = 0.80.
attack.price: The tick-rate carrier coupling (T67/T68) with the tensor books (T64), plus the supplied walk's UV shape (L02-W2) and the sea's zero of energy (T60): the induced strength is a property of the walk and is unusable until the volume term c0 is cancelled.

title: Newton's constant in lattice units and a = l_P are not derived

members.title: The magnitude of Newton's constant in lattice units, and a = l_P, is not derived (three unreconciled candidates)
members.plain: The framework fixes only a ruler: the lattice spacing is set equal to the Planck length by definition of its one reference. Whether its own internal gravity has exactly that strength is called "a separate open gravity derivation". Three routes give three answers: Newton's constant of order the spacing squared over the number of species, exactly 1 under a supplied boundary-count premise, and a free stiffness. None is derived.

members.title: Is the theory's own gravity of strength one in lattice units (a/l_P = 1)?
members.plain: The theory declares its lattice spacing to be the Planck length, as a choice of ruler. What nobody has shown is that the theory's own gravity, measured in that ruler, has strength one. The one route that said yes needs a premise the four axioms do not contain, and a June probe found that premise to be the ruler choice in disguise.

members.title: Newton's constant in lattice units is set by the black-hole match itself, or by a free stiffness
members.plain: The 1/4 fixes the lattice spacing only if gravity's strength in lattice units is known independently. In the notes it is not: the value "Newton's constant = 1" comes from demanding the black-hole match, so the match cannot then test it. The recent gravity work also has a free stiffness number that plays the same role.

attack.plain: The wall is real but half misframed: a/l_P is a dimensionless number of the theory, so no second ruler is needed. In the supplied static model a = l_P is exactly the statement that the curvature-member coefficient K equals 1/(16 pi) (about 0.020; or 1/2 if the ruler means the reduced Planck mass), and nothing in the axioms sets K. Gravity induced by lattice matter gives no single G on a fixed lattice: tensor, conformal and static sectors disagree in size and sign.
attack.best_route: Reframe: treat G_lat as the computed number K (a = l_P <=> K = 1/(16 pi)); first artifact is naming the Planck-mass convention and then deriving K, which is blocked-equivalent to the formation-law and dynamics walls T01/T02.
attack.test: Static model solve on 41-81 boxes: pair energy and test-body energy give G_lat = gamma/(4 pi) = 1/(16 pi K), a factor 2 above the entry; free lattice scalar (exact supercell diagonalisation, checked by perturbation theory): G_TT about 16-20 per scalar, conformal sector G = -0.62, static (n,p) sector G = -4, uniform responses 10^3 times the k^2 terms; entanglement 1/(4c) = 10-13, 1.5x off the induced value.
attack.price: K, the curvature member's stiffness (gamma = 1/(4K)), supplied (block 129); a = l_P is K = 1/(16 pi) [G = l_P^2] or 1/2 [8 pi G = 1]; the induced route additionally needs the metric-DOF posit, a matter-content count and three Planck-size tunings.

title: That gravity attracts (the coupling sign) is not derived

members.title: That gravity attracts (the sign of the coupling) is not derived
members.plain: Nothing in the repository derives that gravity attracts. Three natural arguments, from spectra, from stability and from the arrow of time, do not force it, and stability actually favours repulsion. Each lane reduces the sign to one supplied choice: an orientation datum, whether records slow the clocks around them, or the sign of the size-of-space kinetic term.

attack.plain: Nothing in the repository derives that gravity attracts, but the sign is not a free orientation choice. In the class a fixed lattice with a separate time naturally lives in (Horava/khronometric gravity), Newton's coupling is a computed number, G_N = 2 G_H/(2 xi - eta), and requiring every graviton wave mode to be stable already forces it positive. So the sign comes free with a stable, spatial-curvature-structured graviton (the T64 and T67 targets), while the walker's own vacuum cannot supply it: its clock-field response is concave.
attack.best_route: Horava/khronometric route (Blas-Pujolas-Sibiryakov PRL 104, 181302, eqs. 19 and 22): the sign is a stability corollary; first artifact is the lemma that tensor plus scalar stability implies 0 < eta < 2 xi and hence G_N > 0 (done); wounded because the walker's natural coupling does not give the needed spatial-curvature structure.
attack.test: Three scripts in T71_scratch: (1) sympy re-derivation matching BPS eqs. 19 and 22, 2e6-draw scan (155,151 stable draws, none with G_N <= 0) and a 24^3 lattice solve (Einstein-like, Horava-window and Nordstrom-like cases attract; outside the window and a ground-state conformal channel repel) 9/9; (2) walker-sea curvature on 8^3 and 12^3 tori: <= 0 at every q, q^4 lapse channel, positive log-rate gradient coefficient equals the placement term -E_0/12, TT kappa positive 8/8; (3) ledger threshold: sea alone never binds, uniform stiffness 1.59 (1.33|E_0|) needed 6/6.
attack.price: Stability (no ghost, no gradient instability) of every propagating graviton mode in a spatial-curvature-structured foliation-preserving action (premises P3 with P2); on the ledger route, the supplied sign of the bare field stiffness gamma and of the total vacuum energy (T60). The sign then follows as a corollary (checked at linear order).

title: Universality of free fall holds only under a list of conditions

members.title: Universality of free fall (the equivalence principle) holds only under a list of conditions
members.plain: Gravity must pull every kind of matter the same way. In the lattice lane that holds only under conditions: the curvature member, first order in the field, a particular momentum definition, and for bound groups an extra "binding clause". Some species fall with minus their weight, and records in a clock gradient settle with a weight but do not drift alike.

attack.plain: The wall lists conditions for universal free fall, but where a clock scales a body's whole generator, the question reduces to one number per kind of body, W = rest energy times inverse inertia, which must be 1. Direct simulation confirms this reduction: free walkers and all eight doublers fall alike or fail for single named reasons (speed mismatch, mass entry, momentum-ledger sign), and the diffusive-records drift is not a free-fall test. The composite-body part is not passed: a pair bound by a local contact attraction falls about five times its binding fraction too slowly unless the binding is tuned.
attack.best_route: Replace the list by W = Hess(E^2/2) at rest per body class; the residue is priced by T14 (one speed) and T17 (local books), with boost-algebra closure of the interaction (Dirac/Bakamjian-Thomas) as the outside template.
attack.test: Exact 1D staggered-walker numerics (N=240 singles, N=40/60 pairs, 3D eight-species box): single-walker W within 0.7% of the band value, eight species accelerate identically, pair direct/band 0.989-0.998, pair W-1 = -0.087/-0.247/-0.493 at binding/2m = 0.018/0.061/0.178, tuning kappa* differs per binding (-1.27, -1.37).
attack.cheaper_question: For each stable body class (free species, bound pair, excluded pair), is W = E0 * d2E/dP2 at rest equal to 1 when the clock scales every term of the generator?

title: The axioms define no entropy; five candidates disagree

members.title: The axioms define no entropy; the lane uses five that disagree
members.plain: The axioms give records: permanent, one per site, readable. They give no state vector, no weighting of outcomes and no entropy. The lane has used five different "entropies": a rank count, a count of frozen record patterns, an outcome-weighted entropy, fermion entanglement, and Wald's Noether charge. They disagree. Until the axioms pick one, "entropy = area over four" has no fixed meaning.

attack.plain: The axioms give records but no odds for whole patterns of records and no notion of what counts as 'the same' from outside, and an entropy needs both. On one fixed set of allowed frozen boxes, changing only the formation law moved the entropy by a factor of three in coefficient and across log, surface and volume growth, so choosing among the five candidate entropies cannot fix an area law; the formation measure does. The five are also different kinds of object (a count trace, an ensemble entropy, a wave-state entropy, an action charge), not rival definitions of one thing.
attack.best_route: R3 (misframed): replace 'which entropy' by 'which predecessor structure, kernels and readable partition', then compute S; blocked-equivalent to T01's open choice, with Hartley's ln N (R1) as the only measure-free name and Edwards' flat measure (R2) dead because permanence forbids tapping.
attack.test: Exact enumeration on probe 19's maximal-independent-set boxes: uniform sequential entropy is 0.91 of ln N in 2D (L=4-6, S1/L^2 flat at 0.214), a weight family moves it from 0.29 to 0.97 of ln N at L=5, and three formation laws on the same support give log-class (seed), surface-class (ring, 1/4 per ring site at one bias w*=0.385) and volume-class entropies.
attack.price: The formation measure (site, order, kernels; MINIMAL_AXIOMS:181-184, parked as DEFERRED_DECISIONS:21-48, in the block-16 form 'which neighbours are already written') plus the observability partition (MINIMAL_AXIOMS:185-186); without a measure only Hartley's ln N remains, which needs the additivity cut on 2026-08-13 and an unspecified support map.

title: The black-hole 1/4 is a supplied count (BP); entanglement gives 1/6 without a selector

members.title: The 1/4 is a count of a supplied cell, not an entropy, and is not tied to gravity (BP)
members.plain: The framework's "1/4" is a counting fact: 4 of the 16 states of a four-slot cell the notes supply. Black-hole entropy is a different kind of number: entropy per unit of horizon area. Nobody has shown from the axioms that the count is the entropy, or that this cell has anything to do with gravity. The notes call this the bridge premise (BP) and leave it open.

members.title: Exactly 1/4 from entanglement needs a hand-picked selector, and the natural law has a logarithm
members.plain: If the entropy is the entanglement of ordinary lattice fermions, the natural answer is one sixth of the boundary times a logarithm of the size, not one quarter. Getting exactly 1/4 needs a hand-picked extra ingredient (a half-filled zone, a two-band edge, a special edge probability), each a tuning knob. A finite-state edge built from algebraic numbers cannot give exactly 1/4 at all.

members.title: The lane's own numerical test cannot yet tell 1/4 from 1/6; part of the excess is a zero-mode effect
members.plain: The lane's own numerical test looks close to 1/4 at the sizes tried (0.257 at size 64), but the number is still falling. Fit it one way and it heads to 1/4, another way to 1/6. My rerun shows about half of the excess over 1/6 at size 40 comes from a mixed-state device used to handle degenerate zero-energy states. The proof that would settle the limit does not exist.

attack.plain: The black-hole 1/4 is two separate claims glued together. The action side only says a unit-normalisation constant b equals 1, which is Newton's constant in lattice units (T70), because the notes let b and G rescale together. The entropy side compares the wrong quantities: the repo's own half-filled sea has an area coefficient of 0.197 to 0.231 depending on cut direction, never 1/4, so there is no single entanglement number to match.
attack.best_route: R3: replace both 1/4 targets by 'what fixes G_lat (equivalently b) against the matter action?' (T70/T64); with an Einstein-Hilbert action S = A/4G follows by Wald for any G.
attack.test: Computed the area-law entropy per unit Euclidean area of the pi-flux cubic sea (torus L=8..20 and transverse-momentum slab chains): eta = 0.1967/0.2173/0.2308 for (100)/(110)/(111) at m=0 (17% spread), falls with mass (0.1647 at m=1), never reaches 1/4; pre-registered FAIL. Exact algebra check: G_lat*b invariant under b -> lambda*b.
attack.cheaper_question: What fixes the coefficient of the gravitational action (b = 1/G_lat) relative to the matter action in lattice units? Once an Einstein-Hilbert action exists, S = A/4G holds for any G by Wald, and matter entanglement is expected to renormalise G rather than equal 1/4.

title: No lattice horizon and no lattice Hawking radiation

members.title: No lattice derivation of a horizon; the thermodynamics is standard general relativity on an assumed surface
