members.plain: Black-hole thermodynamics in the notes (Hawking temperature, first law, Bekenstein bound) is standard general relativity on a smooth spacetime that is assumed, not derived from the lattice. Lattice results point the other way: clocks slow but never stop, older strong-field runs find a floor, not a horizon, and the tensor-gravity probes find no clean light-speed graviton. What a black hole is in this framework is unsettled.

members.title: Hawking radiation has no lattice derivation; the one lattice test failed and was retracted
members.plain: Hawking radiation appears only as a temperature formula borrowed from smooth spacetime. The one lattice test (a "Hawking analog") gave amplification instead of trapping, and its temperature-versus-gravity sign was wrong; its headline was retracted. A real evaporation model also needs something that traps and then leaks, which permanent records and unitary evolution do not obviously allow. Nobody has built one.

attack.plain: A thermal law T = kappa/2pi does hold on the framework's own unitary clocked walker once a local clock rate has a linear zero, so the earlier failed Hawking analog is not a framework obstruction. But the record dynamics does not supply a linear zero: for every smooth scale-covariant stiffness energy a large stopped region has a double zero, so kappa = 0 and the lattice black hole has no Hawking temperature. A clock stops at finite mass only for one bond energy and only at a single site (m* = 18/gamma).
attack.best_route: R1 lattice Unruh (horizon = zero of local speed on a unitary chain, thermality from vacuum entanglement) for the kinematics; the dynamical half needs a linear lapse zero, i.e. a master clock or a metric degree of freedom (T64/T67).
attack.test: Diamond-geometry Planck plot on the clocked chain gave beta/pi = 1.0063..1.0033 (N = 100..800, R^2 >= 0.99996; the pre-registered wedge version missed at 0.775); second bond energy reaches a stopped clock at m* = 18/gamma on 41^3 (ratio 74.63 vs 74.81); 1D exponents p -> 2 for three weight-one energies, p = 1 only for weight two.
attack.price: Weight-one (scale-covariant, no master clock) smooth nearest-neighbour rate stiffness on the fixed flat lattice: it forces a double lapse zero (kappa = 0, T_H = 0); a finite Hawking temperature needs a weight-two stiffness (master clock) or a metric degree of freedom (T64/T67). Label: suggested.

title: The frozen-box black hole: no formation rule, volume not area, clause C1, no holography

members.title: The owner's frozen-box reading has no formation rule and the count grows with volume, not area
members.plain: The owner's picture: a sealed box fills with records until nothing more can form, and a frozen box is a black hole. Black-hole entropy grows with surface area, but a box of records grows with volume. With the simple formation rules tested, the number of possible frozen boxes is either one or grows with volume. The axioms give no formation rule, so the rule that matters is untested.

members.title: Frozen box versus black-hole entropy: no rule and no identified entropy
members.plain: The owner's picture: a box fills with records until it is frozen, and a frozen box is a black hole. Black-hole entropy grows with the area. For the simplest crowding rules the number of possible frozen states grows with the volume instead, and for other rules it is unknown or unique. Which rule, and which quantity counts as entropy, are not fixed.

members.title: Clause C1 (every site's clock ticks at a positive rate) conflicts with the owner's stopped-clock (frozen-box) reading
members.plain: The source-link lane assumes every site's clock ticks at a positive rate, which rules out a stopped clock. The owner's reading, that a box which can form no more records is frozen and that time is the making of records, needs a rate that can reach zero, as at a horizon. As they stand, the two readings do not fit together.

members.title: Holography has no bridge; the one gravity-specific fit failed and the language was stripped
members.plain: The idea that a region's information lives on its boundary was probed in April with a free-fermion lattice and a toy gravity coupling. Boundary scaling appeared, but standard theorems already guarantee that for free fermions. The one gravity-specific formula (entropy proportional to one over the coupling) fit badly, so the holography language was removed from the note.

attack.plain: No supplied formation rule gives a frozen box whose number of states grows with surface area. In 2D all but one count-threshold rule have a local switch and so a volume-law count; the one exception (form unless exactly one neighbour is recorded) looked boundary-determined to L = 10 but gains interior swaps from L = 11. Record contents may add volume to any rule, so the entropy has to be fixed before the rule search matters.
attack.best_route: Check whether Admissibility's contents menu is a singleton on frozen states (hours); if not, ask whether the exterior-visible shell count is the entropy meant; occupation-rule search (rigid rule E) is nearly dead.
attack.test: Gadget classification of all 2D and 3D count-threshold rules (14 of 15 non-trivial 2D rules volume-law, verified by construction) plus exact reachable counts for rule E to L = 13 (N = 2399) and shell-determination test: one completion per outer shell to L = 10, two from L = 11.

title: Balance-law (Gauss/ice) patterns are not outputs of local formation and break covariance

members.title: Gauss-law (ice-rule) states are not outputs of directed local formation
members.plain: The 'photon from a neighbourhood constraint' route needs states where every vertex obeys a balance rule (the ice rule). Tested as the outcome of records forming one after another from local information, no local order, rule or record scheme produces it. The exceptions add a coordinator site or a non-local plan. A balance rule constrains both sides of a neighbourhood at once, while formation reads only the earlier side.

members.title: The link-and-role pattern breaks the axioms' one-qubit-everywhere covariance, and nearest-neighbour formation cannot build it
members.plain: The photon model puts qubits only on sites with exactly one odd coordinate and uses the rest as bookkeeping. The axioms have a qubit at every site and full cubic symmetry. A nearest-neighbour formation rule cannot make sites obey a balance rule around a neighbour: the chance of a completed pattern is at most 5/16 for the ice rule when formation order is arbitrary and the rule is unsoldered.

members.title: Forces as balance-law patterns: the lane's covariant clause cannot move them, and Admissibility is not shown to be such a law
members.plain: Forces such as light are naturally patterns that obey a balance rule at every site. But any rule built only from neighbouring pairs, including the Heisenberg bond (the only pair rule that treats all qubit directions alike), leaves such a pattern frozen. Moving it needs four-link loops or three-site hops that the axioms do not supply. One qubit also cannot carry a covariant charge or a non-abelian link. So "Admissibility as a balance law" is a hope, not a derivation.

attack.plain: Local formation can build a defect-free balance pattern (Gauss/ice rule) only if the order in which sites form is itself a sharp 3-earlier / 3-later front, so the balance law moves from the pattern into the formation order; random, badly jittered or closed orders leave 3-17% defects, and random ones do not screen. Separately, giving every site the same balance rule leaves a deterministic recursion with no bulk entropy, so the photon model's typed roles cannot come from covariance. The uniform-measure half of the wall is untouched.
attack.best_route: R1: the lane's own sweep (3 back, 3 forward) with the necessity lemma and price stated as a note; the order premise is where the wall lands.
attack.test: Test A: exact balance at every site has 140 patterns on the 4-torus, 0 on the 6-torus, 4x4xn transfer spectral radius 1.0 (zero bulk entropy, proved by five neighbours fixing the sixth); Test B: sweep orders 0 defects, random order 16.4%, closed torus defects x L = 0.33, jitter 0 up to sigma 0.15 then 0.4-12.5%.
attack.price: A sharp formation order with three earlier and three later neighbours at every vertex (the arrow of formation obeys the same balance law), plus a supplied role pattern; uniform measure not passed.

title: The photon's light-speed dispersion in the qubit-link model is not established

members.title: The photon's light-speed dispersion in the qubit-link model is not established
members.plain: With an ice rule and square-loop flips on link qubits, the evidence says a wave exists that costs almost nothing at long wavelength. Whether its energy grows in step with wavenumber, like light, or with its square, is undecided. The methods in use give only upper limits on that energy, never a lower limit, so a slow mode with small weight cannot be ruled out.

attack.plain: Nobody has shown that the lightest transverse wave of the ice-rule qubit-link model has energy proportional to wavenumber, and no ground-state method can show it, because those methods only give upper limits on the wave's energy. Near the Rokhsar-Kivelson point the electric stiffness that would make the wave light-like reduces to a classical counting number; I measured it to 32^3 and it does not shrink. The remaining obligations, that the lowest level really is that wave and that the phase is stable, are as hard as the wall itself.
attack.best_route: R1: expand about the RK point (E_C = -eps<N_f>_C + O(eps^2)); the flux-sector stiffness is a classical number, c_L about 1.6 to L = 32, then fix the O(eps^2) uniformity in L and add a sign-free QMC imaginary-time C(tau,k) check (R2) for the lowest level.
attack.test: Pre-registered classical Monte Carlo of the uniform ice ensemble in fixed flux sectors (validated on L = 2 against exact enumeration): c_L = 1.645, 1.622, 1.601, 1.563, 1.558, 1.615, 1.567 for L = 4 to 32, exponent p = 0.012 +/- 0.020, pre-registered pass; second-order coefficient per site saturates at about 0.23.

title: The Maxwell dynamics class is supplied

members.title: The Maxwell dynamics class is supplied, including energy conservation and the time rule
members.plain: Grant the ice rule. The photon's equations of motion (electric and magnetic fields updating by curl equations, energy conserved, time continuous) are still chosen. Within that choice Maxwell's equations are the unique answer, with one free speed. The choice itself is not derived, and the repo lists three competing ways to discretise time.

attack.plain: The Maxwell class cannot come from the four axioms because they contain no time, but it is fewer separate gaps than listed: conserved energy is the same as no runaway in either time direction, keeping the ice rule invariant removes the vertex and cube extras, and the time-rule fork is one friction rate that must be exactly zero. What is left is exact reversibility of the unrecorded field, one real component per link with no coin, and one-neighbour reach. The class is also only the small-oscillation limit of a conservative law, so its real content sits in the dynamics-clause wall (T02) and the photon-dispersion wall (T78).
attack.best_route: R1 plus R3: replace item 6 by neutral stability (no field runs away in either time direction) with both Gauss rows held as invariants; the class then rests on exact reversibility, payload count and locality.
attack.test: test_T79.py: on a 59,049-member grid at side 4, bounded orbits leave exactly 26 nonzero members and exactly 2 (Maxwell, one speed) with both Gauss rows, as pre-registered; friction, cube-exit and rotor-Hessian checks also passed (first rotor run failed on a script bug, fixed and rerun).
attack.price: Exact reversibility of the unrecorded field evolution (no runaway in either time direction, friction exactly 0), together with one-real-per-link payload and one-neighbour reach; conditionally supplied by the 2026-09-24 reversibility note in the harmonic regime only.

title: Record dynamics keeps adding free dimensionless constants

members.title: The record-dynamics lane keeps adding free dimensionless constants
members.plain: The axioms give no numbers for how strongly neighbouring records affect one another. The September work on moving records keeps finding one more free number: an overall binding scale, the gravity-like stiffness, the ratio that sets how fast field waves travel, a formation rate. The owner calls the binding scale "a primitive like planck". A proposal to fix it by a no-privilege argument exists but is not adopted, and the proof of long-range order does not reach that value.

members.title: The motion rule of moving records and the new binding constant
members.plain: In the owner's picture records hop to neighbouring empty sites 'when the neighbourhood allows'. Two readings of 'allows' give different physics. One has the static law as equilibrium and records that clump. The other has an arrow inside the motion and no clumping. The clumping strength is a new dimensionless number that the axioms' normalized odds cannot see.

attack.plain: T80 glues one real number, the binding scale c (how much more a record beside a record weighs than a record beside an empty site, invisible to the axioms' odds), to a list of numbers that belong to the gravity member and the formation-rate walls. In a simulation of the ordered record gas, at equal record density the order and the stiffness do not depend on c or the fugacity (0.2% agreement), and the neutral pin c = c0 still orders at ordinary parameters, so the proofs' 'further number' is a technique limit. What is left open is what sets the record density, which is formation history.
attack.best_route: R2: infrared data depend on (c, z) only through the record density (lattice-gas map and RG universality); fallback R1: pin c = c0 as the reading 'crowding alone is neutral'.
attack.test: Heat-bath Monte Carlo of the sphere-menu vacancy gas (L = 8, 12): orders at c = c0 with Binder crossing beta_c about 0.74 (z = 10) and 0.96 (z = 3); order parameter and helicity modulus agree between c0 and c = 1 at matched density to at most 0.0015 and 0.21% (rho 0.93-0.998); exact checks of the loop-gas identity, interface-tension identity and mass-channel formula pass.
attack.cheaper_question: Does any infrared observable of the ordered record gas depend on anything but the rule's weights and the record density (checked: no, sphere menu, rho >= 0.93), and what sets the density (formation history, T01/T16)?

title: Ordered-phase thresholds are proved far from where they are observed

members.title: Ordered-phase thresholds are proved far from where they are observed
members.plain: Does the formation law keep a memory of direction (an ordered phase)? Numerically yes above a modest coupling (about 11). The landed theorem proves it only from about 285,000; the campaign's record quotes 4165, and a refereed, unlanded probe gets 84. The natural proof route was refuted, and the campaign advises stopping. For the sphere version no ordered phase was found.

attack.plain: The ordered-phase gap is a proof-technique gap on a supplied law, not a blocker: the best landed proof is p >= 4165 (not 285718), a sharper unlanded count gives 84, and the dominating automaton every proof uses itself only orders near p = 19 while the real law orders near 10.75-11. The theorems also assume a supplied, non-rotation-invariant formation order and a free coupling, and no landed note consumes the ordered phase, so the sharp threshold is bookkeeping unless something pins the coupling between 5.1 and 4165.
attack.best_route: Land the refinement-history count (p >= 84, exact floor 83.6); going lower needs an erosion-based renormalization method, not a better count.
attack.test: Exact certificates re-verified; simulation gave onset of the dominating automaton at p about 19-19.5 (L up to 384, 12000 levels) and of the actual law at 10.75-11; a worst-case all-ones-boundary window fills at every p from 25 to 150.
attack.cheaper_question: Does any landed result place the formation-law coupling in (5.1, 4165) or require direction memory, given that the level order is a supplied clause (T01) and the coupling is free (T02)? If not, the usable content is 'unique for p <= 5.1; ordered under the supplied level order for p >= 4165'.
